### Vehicle themes: the family layer brought back for the race machines

The vehicle family layer (`meta-fabricator.js`) was built to fill airports and streets with variations of the old nets'
vehicles. Its ideas now serve the race machines: a family's types, its decoration as data, and how a series is sampled.
The cars and parts are templates. A THEME is how a user makes one their own: a card of what it is painted, finished and
dressed in, worn by a cartoon racer or a supercar alike, varied across a field, and lit by the seventh generation.
No release has carried the race machines, so their recipes took the new key freely. The old nets' families and their
`vehicle-instance` rows are as they were.

- **The theme card** (`car-designer/vehicle-theme.js`):
  - `palette`: by slot (body, skin, trim, accent, frame, glass, seat, tyre, the driver's suit and helmet).
  - `finish`: the form render's material rows.
    - The paint: gloss, satin, matte, metallic, pearl (three's iridescence) or candy.
    - The trim's metal: alloy, chrome, brass, gold, copper, gunmetal or black. It also colours the trim where the
      palette names none, and a gloss wheel's lip and boss.
    - The colours that glow (`glow: ['accent', 'skin']`), each in its own colour.
  - `livery`, and `shape`: the vehicle sheet's facets the racer is read with.
  - `prefer`: the parts a racer's solver reaches for, or null to leave an optional family off.
  - `supercar`: the supercar's own words (cabin, headlights, vents, spoiler, preset).
  - `vary`: how a series varies it.
  - **Written three ways:**
    - a starter's name: `candy`, `steampunk`, `neon`, `military`, `royal`, `heritage`, each a distinct look;
    - a card of the user's own;
    - a card over a starter: `{ from: 'steampunk', palette: { body: '#20304a' } }`.
    - Every word is checked, and an error names the known ones.
  - **A series:** the k-th car is the theme with its hues turned within the theme's spread. The same turn applies to
    every colour, so the harmony holds; the trim's metal never turns, and its liveries come in turn. Car 0 is the theme
    itself, and `{ from, variant }` names any other.
- **On a cartoon racer** (`racer.js`, `roster.js`; a recipe's `theme`):
  - **Reading:** the theme's shape and livery are read in place of the driver's, each with its reason.
  - **Parts:** the solver ranks the theme's parts ahead of the fits, and a pin still wins. The laws still judge and
    advise: a theme can leave one advised, and the readout says so.
  - **Paint:** the palette goes on the slots, over the outfit's.
  - **Finish:** the material rows the page lights it with. A colour that glows is its own material (`glow:accent`,
    `glow:skin`), shining as a lamp does, unshaded.
  - **A roster in a `series`:** each racer without its own theme wears the next variation. The balance lean swaps a
    family the theme names only for another of the theme's own parts.
- **On a supercar** (`supercar-figure.js` `supercarOfSpec`; a spec's `theme`):
  - The palette is its paint and its livery's second colour, under the spec's own surface words.
  - The trim's metal goes on its alloy.
  - A glowing skin lights its stripes in the form render.
- **In a quick race:**
  - `series` themes the whole field of racers or supercars, each car its own variation.
  - A supercar entry takes its own `theme`, and a themed car is painted by it, not by the solved liveries.
- **The family layer, version 2** (`meta-fabricator.js`):
  - **The families:** `racer` (the parts grammar; its types the driver archetypes) and `supercar` (the surface
    compiler; its types the library's cards) sit beside the nets' four. Their decoration kind is `theme`.
  - **Describing:** `describeFamily` gives an authoring surface the types, the starters, the finishes, a card's keys
    and (the racer's) the parts vocabulary a theme prefers from.
  - **Sampling:** draws a recipe on the dice it is given.
  - **Building:** loads the race machines only when one is built (`car-designer/race-families.js`), so it is
    asynchronous.
  - **Previewing:** a `vehicle-instance` takes `{ racer }` or `{ supercar }`, so `mint_solid { kind: 'vehicle' }`
    previews a themed race machine on the studio grid, with its light painted in.
  - **Docs:** the `vehicle` solid card and the `design-vehicle-family` catalyst say how a user writes a theme: no
    source edit, no registry row.
- **Held** (`vehicle-theme.test.js`, `meta-fabricator.test.js`). Each concept is tested on a starter chosen in code by
  what it carries:
  - the card read and refused;
  - a series' variation;
  - the finish's rows;
  - on a racer: the theme's shape, its preferred parts under a pin, a family left off, its palette, its finish and the
    glowing colours, and no key without a theme;
  - a roster in a series, and the lean keeping to the theme's parts;
  - on a supercar: paint, livery, the spec's surface over the theme's, the trim's metal and the glowing stripe;
  - the quick race's words;
  - the families described, sampled on the dice, built, previewed and refused.
  - No theme: every figure as it was.
- **Seen:** `scripts/render-themes.mjs` renders each starter on a racer, two of its series' variations and a supercar
  in the lit material review. The eyes gate is open.
- **Not built, said:**
  - A theme's own part (a block card in the user's recipe, beside the library's rows).
  - A race reading a user's previewed vehicle by its ref.
  - The studio grid drawing the form render: the preview paints its light in, and the finish shows in the race.

### Architect mode: a house built for what it is for, a game read at a glance or a show at its best

The scene composer's first question is what a place is for. A house carries `purpose: 'game' | 'show'`, stamped at
mint (`era/compose-purpose.js`): a `level` is a game, any other house a show, and a house minted before purposes is
built as it was, byte for byte.

- **The game's rail: readability, never face overdrive.** Each piece is drawn from its own faces at a coarser grain
  (`scene/readable-rung.js`: vertices snapped to the mean of a 7.5 cm cell, collapsed faces gone, shared vertices still
  shared), whatever made it, and nothing is set on a table. A room's pieces are laid in rank within an allowance of
  faces (`allowance: { room }`, the rail's by default): what the room is for (the bed, the sofa, the kitchen run)
  always stands, the rest while the allowance holds, a cheap piece tried after a costly one is left out. The World
  reads the spend as `rails`, room by room, with what each left out and a room over its allowance said. A furnished
  two-storey villa falls from 36,464 faces to 10,329, its furniture from about 31,000 to 4,900.
- **The show's rail: fidelity.** Every piece as its maker drew it, every table set: the house as it always was.

### Beast style: the cover's qualities, and oozes on the beast-kin

The seventh generation's cover had one look per kind, while the older generations gave a coat style qualities: the
egocube creature's cell sizes, scutes and feather rows; the fauna's coats. The animal door's oozes (frost, venom, dire,
transmetal …) styled only a species' ring plan. This theme carries both onto the beast-kin.

- **The cover's qualities** (`beast/cover.js` `COVER_STYLE`; `beast.cover: { kind, length?, size?, shape?, sheen?,
  tipped? }`):
  - fur: `length` short, plush (the default) or shaggy;
  - scales: `size` fine, medium or large, and `shape` round or keeled (a ridge down each scale); chitin and feathers:
    `size` small, medium or large;
  - any cover: `sheen` matte, satin (the kind's own), glossy or metal (the material's metal channel full), and
    `tipped` 0 … 1 (the coat darkened toward its roots, its crests light: frosted or banded tips).

  Each word moves its tile; a cover named by its kind alone is the tile as it was, byte for byte. The door refuses a
  quality its kind does not take, by name.
- **Oozes on the beast-kin** (`beast/ooze.js`, `beast/style.js`; `beast.ooze`, `beast.seed`). The animal door's word
  and its composition law: a word, or a list of words and `{ id, strength }`, composed by `mutagen/compose.js` and
  `push.js` as for an animal, then lowered onto the beast's anatomy:
  - its growth onto the masses (bulk, legBulk, the wedge's fore and hind, the neck, the limbs, the paws), each
    multiplier read at half its strength on an upright body (`UPRIGHT_MASS`: a dire animal's chest ×1.45 swelled an
    upright trunk into a barrel); its `headScale` onto the head;
  - its colour layers (darken, desaturate, saturate, tints) onto the coat, before the head is dressed in it;
  - hackles, plates or tail spikes as a crest of spines in a group of its own (`Spines`), in the hackles' or the
    motif's colour, glowing and of the motif's material as the row says; a ruff as the ruff;
  - the motif onto the claws' tone, glow and material; the eyes' colour onto the head's iris, a glow lighting it;
    the head's skull and muzzle pushes as the designed head's row moves, its eye grown; its expression added;
  - a recoloured group where the body or its head has it (transmetal's chrome faceplate on the library head's
    `Skull` and `Snout`), its surfaces; a colour word (`accent`, `suit` …) against the coat, as for an animal;
  - a new `cover` push on the rows (frost's rimed glossy tips, crystal's glass, transmetal's metal, venom's wet gloss,
    shadow's and zombie's matte, dire's shagginess) onto the cover's qualities, the ones its kind takes. An animal
    reads none of it: its oozes emit as before.

  A word the hero names itself stands over the ooze's. What the tiered body does not carry yet is named in the
  lowering's `pending`: the ooze's `scale` (the tiered body's size is its tune's stature), horns, fangs, ears, pistons,
  armour, and the marks.
- **The marks are not painted on the biped.** The fauna's markings (band, belly, stripes, patch, spots) are windows in
  a quadruped's frame: `t` from the spine down to the belly, `run` from the rump to the chest. Painted onto the upright
  body's rings they read inside out (a glowing belly became a bib over the whole front, flank stripes hoops), and the
  rings are too coarse for a pattern finer than a ring. They wait for a biped's own pattern solver.

Machine gate (`beast/ooze.test.js`): each cover word moves its tile and the default does not; an ooze tones the coat,
raises a glowing crest in its own group, lights the eyes and styles the cover, deterministic, the hero's word standing;
a composition grows the masses at the upright power, its pending named; a recoloured head group lands; the door's
refusals; an oozed beast binds and rigs whole. The presets' pin is unchanged (`beast/composer.char.test.js`). Eyes: one
wolf-kin through frost, fire, venom, dire with half venom, shadow, transmetal and zombie (the operator's to judge).

### The biped's coat: patterns solved in an upright body's anatomy, painted into an atlas

The animal door's markings are windows in a quadruped's frame, and on the tiered body's rings they read inside out (the
previous theme withdrew them). This theme gives the biped a pattern solver of its own and a texture to paint it in.

- **The solver** (`beast/pattern.js`; `beast.pattern`: a list of layers, a later one over an earlier). Each layer is a
  field over the body's rest surface in metres, read in the biped's anatomy:
  - a point's region (trunk, neck, arm, leg, tail, coil);
  - its dorsality: the trunk's and the neck's back against their front, a limb's outer face against its inner one, a
    tail's top against its underside;
  - its angle round from the spine, its height on the trunk, and its distance down its limb, in metres from the
    limb's root so a band runs on across the knee.

  The layers:
  - `countershade`: the light underside (throat, chest and belly, the inner arms and thighs, under the tail);
  - `stripes`: chevrons swept down and forward from the spine round the flanks, thinning and stopping short of the
    front, a wobble of their own; bands across the limbs' outer faces; rings round the tail;
  - `spots` and `rosettes` (a broken dark ring round a darkened centre) on a jittered lattice in metres, fewer toward
    the front;
  - `points` (the extremities darkened), `socks`, `saddle` (a dark field over the back), `dorsal` (a line down the
    spine).

  Colours are hex or the coat's own words (suit, armor, seam, accent, opposite); lengths scale with the body; the
  fields are mirror-symmetric and deterministic. The door refuses a layer or a word by name.
- **The coat as an atlas** (`beast/coat-atlas.js` `beastCoatPaint`). The pattern is painted in colour into one texture
  over the coat, at texel density (240 a metre at a 1.8 m figure), so a stripe is as fine as it is drawn, never a
  ring's: a thigh has six rings, a neck three. It is laid out as the hide atlas is (`skin-paint.js`: every coat part
  its own rectangle, the UV of a vertex read off its id) and lit as the realistic skin is (`heroSkinPaint`: the texel
  carries the colour, the face's light divided by the coat's colour lights it, so it is never tinted twice), so the
  World page draws it and the skinned GLB carries it by the same path (`world-kinds.js`). A beast with no pattern:
  none, as before.
- **The cover's relief on the atlas** (`coatRelief`). One UV set carries the paint, so the cover's tiling map gave way
  to it. Instead, the cover tile's normals (the cover's kind and its qualities) are laid into each part's rectangle in
  metres, at twice the atlas's density, box-filtered to the map's texel, each painted corner its tangent on the atlas's
  UVs; the pack carries it as the realistic skin's relief (`normalTex`). Not carried yet on a patterned coat: the
  cover's occlusion, roughness and metal (its sheen) and its tipped crests, which ride the tiling map only.
- **The hero viewer's cameras** (`.claude/skills/hero-live`): a full-body side view and a back view (`vBodySide`,
  `vBack`), for a coat's back and a tail.

Machine gate (`beast/pattern.test.js`): each layer's law on samples (the front lightened and the back not, stripes
from
the spine and none at the front, a limb's outer face only, the tail ringed, points toward a limb's end, the spine alone,
mirror symmetry), the refusals; the atlas absent without a pattern, deterministic, the coat's faces alone, a stripe
finer than a leg's rings; the relief at its scale with a tangent on every painted corner. Eyes: a tabby cat-kin, a
rosetted cat-kin and a saddled wolf-kin, front, back, side and bust, in the exported GLB (the operator's to judge).

### Trees of leaves in hands

- **A broadleaf's crown as crossed bundles** (`vegetation/twigs.js`, the operator's designs). Each leaf is a few
  triangles of its outline (`LEAF_TRIS`): a maple's four (two big triangles facing each other, their slopes crossing to
  its two middle points, a pointed one on each slope), an oak's four (a tall kite in two halves, two wide triangles across
  it whose corners are the lobes), a willow's three (long narrow blades fanned from one base), a beech's or cherry's
  pointed oval, a broad leaf's round one. A clump is a HAND of them (`CROSS.bundle`: 21 maple leaves; by outline as many
  as hold the maple's cover), one card a leaf, each its own finger: its tip 25–70° out of the crown, round it as its
  place in the bundle is, its face the one most out of the crown, rolled up to 60° askew and tipped a little to the sun.
  Two leaves crossed on one midrib covered little more than one; turned each its own way, two thirds of the cards hold
  the crossed bundle's cover (0.91–1.0 of it seen from round the crown's outside, its worst view 0.85–1.06), each leaf
  8% larger. None spills past the clump's room. A new species, the maple (Rauh's
  rhythm, its limbs sweeping round and a little crooked), joins beech and oak among the trail's defaults.
- **Leaves where the branches are** (`form/tree-form.js`, `twigs`). A crossed crown's bundles sit on its shoots, not in
  its envelope: one a cell of the crown (`SHOOTS.cell`, set so a crown draws a fifth fewer twigs, each bundle a few
  leaves fuller), on the leafy node standing furthest out in it, facing out from the crown and
  along its twig (`crossClumps`). The twig a bundle sits on is drawn, and so are the limbs it grows on, three-sided when
  thin; a twig carrying no bundle is not drawn. A sparse crown's cell narrows until it carries at least forty bundles
  (`SHOOTS.least`), so a thin tree is leafed along its twigs rather than only at their ends. Leaves point outward and
  sideways, not down; every triangle of a leaf winds the same way, so overlapping pieces no longer flicker. A species can
  name the seed its trail tree grows from (`specimen`: beech and willow 5, a full crown where seed 1 grows a thin one).
- **A grown tree's stance** (`form/tree-form.js`). A broadleaf now stands as a grown tree: its limbs below a quarter
  of its height shed (20–30% by its seed), its leaves from 30% up, drawn in to 80% of its spread, and each tree its own
  spread, bare stem and lean by its seed. Its near leaves are its crosses (no sprays); a needled crown keeps its clumps
  and sprays. A weeping crown keeps its curtains, and a bundle standing alone (a dangler) is dropped.
- **Far off, the same tree** (`form/flora-read.js`, `scene/channels/form-flora.js`). A crossed crown's far level keeps
  its near wood, every branch and the trunk as they were, and every bundle where it stands with half its leaves, larger
  (`FLORA_LOD.half`): the switch changes neither the branches nor the outline (held at about 0.9 of the near one). Up
  close, at 12 m, an oak is about 4.9k wood and 7k leaf triangles, a maple 3.1k and 3.9k, a beech 2.1k and 10k; the
  forest trail's trailhead view draws about 460k flora triangles.
- **To scale on the trail** (`form/flora-read.js`). A crossed broadleaf on a trail grows at its species' own heights
  and a quarter more (`FLORA_TALL`: beech 12.5–22.5 m, oak 14–25, maple 12.5–22.5), each tree where it ranks among the
  level's heights, its first limbs past two people's heights (4.3–5.2 m at the level's middle tree), so its crown
  stands over a walker's head as a grown tree's does; the painted level's heights (a forest's 8–14 m) put its lowest
  leaves at eye height. Needled crowns, bamboo and bushes keep the level's heights.
- **No ghost leaves** (`scene/channels/creases.js`, `scene/channels/form-flora.js`). The contact occlusion's prepass drew
  every plant where it would stand without wind, so a pale copy of each swaying leaf and twig showed beside it against the
  sky. A material that moves its vertices now names its own vertex shader for the prepass (`userData.prepass`), and the
  plants' bark, leaves, culms and blossom name their wind and a spray's growth: the occlusion falls where the frame
  draws them. A page without such a material draws every mesh in the prepass as before.

### Desert dunes

- **A trail's land laid in sand dunes** (`era/out-dunes.js`, a trail's `ground.dunes: true | { height?, spacing?, wind?,
  repose?, supply?, sinuous? }`). The shape real dunes take, not a noise's: across the wind a dune rises over a long back and
  rounds to its brink, then falls down its slip face at dry sand's angle of repose (`repose`, 32°; so a taller dune's face
  is longer) and eases out at its foot. The crests run across the wind (`wind` in degrees, 0 across the trail), wandering (`sinuous`); where the sand is
  plenty (`supply`) they are long transverse ridges, where it thins they break into crescents whose horns trail downwind.
  Laid over the ground once the walk and the edits are (`era/out-trail.js`), easing to nothing toward the walk (from 1.5 to
  8 m past its edge: the walk keeps a firm inter-dune street and its grade), the far cliff's foot, a pocket and its spur, a
  ford and the site's edges; the mounds lie down where the sand stands. Their sand is cut into the ground along its own
  line through the troughs (`isekai:sand`), no grass on it, no stone placed on it (the site's `clear`). Absent, or
  `false`, adds nothing: the same ground to the byte.
- **The cube's dunes** (`outside.dunes`, the same words): every trail the cube paints takes them, a scene's path and a
  game's levels alike; a trail's own win, its `false` refuses them (`era/geocube.js`, as its water).
- **In words.** "dunes" and "dune" lay the cube's dunes on an open land (no far cliff) in the desert biome; "erg" the
  sea of sand (full supply, 4 m crests); "sandy" a thinner field of crescents. They no longer turn the trail's bumpiness
  up (the mounds would ruffle the sand). "desert" alone keeps its rock desert, no dunes. The geocube manual and the
  `scene` routing card say so.
- **Their sand drawn by the wind, in gen-7** (`scene/channels/form-land.js`, the form read's `dunes`: `era/out-dunes.js`
  duneMap, the wind and a metre map of where the dunes stand and their crests). On the dunes' backs and the flats between,
  ripples run across the wind about 11 cm apart, gentle on their upwind side and steep on their downwind side, their
  spacing wandering over a couple of metres so crests merge and fork, a shade paler at each crest; they fade before they
  alias, and the sand's own tile is calmed under them. A slip face carries none: its sand avalanches in streaks down the
  fall line. A grain in a hundred, a centimetre across, is turned its own way and polished, so the sun catches it as glint
  through the light (lit and shadowed by it, never drawn over it). The shape near the eye needed no more: the land's
  half-metre mesh, shaded smooth, holds a dune's curve and its brink. A land with no dunes carries none of this: the
  same page to the byte.

### Facial mocap simulator: the realistic hero acts

The realistic hero's face as a facial capture session records it: per-frame curves in ARKit's 52 blendshapes, written
by a simulator from a performance described in words (the lines, the beats, the gaze, the intensity), so the hero can
say a line and play a scene, and play a real phone capture through the same controls. The eyes gate is the operator's.

- **The vocabulary** (`face-acting/facs.js`): FACS's action units as the face's controls, each with its muscle, its
  side, its ARKit names (the 52, each read through the AU it captures) and the realistic head's action that makes it,
  or a gap said by name; the basic emotions as FACS's prototypes (EMFACS) at its intensities; `facsActions(state)` turns
  a face's AUs into the head's actions and returns what it cannot make, never another unit in its place.
- **The face's missing muscles** (`head-relational.js` `ACTIONS`): the outer brow raised alone (AU2), the cheek raised
  (AU6), the nose wrinkled (AU9: the nostrils and wings drawn up, the brows' inner ends down), the upper lip raised (AU10),
  the dimple (AU14), the mouth's corners pulled down (AU15), the lower lip drawn down (AU16), the chin raised (AU17: the
  mentalis pushes the lower lip up, the chin's bone stays), the lips stretched (AU20), tightened (AU23) and pressed (AU24),
  each per side where FACS splits it, and the brows lowered, the eyes widened and squinted per side. Every one of FACS's
  basic emotion prototypes now builds on the realistic head. A head with none of them keeps its bytes.
- **Their targets** (`relational-face-rig.js`): the realistic face's morph targets grow from 9 to one per unit and side
  (each unit's build, a sided one split across the midline, the smile and the eyes' too), and `facsWeights(state)`
  weighs a FACS state onto them, the jaw (a bone) said apart. The rig is rebuilt for every realistic hero on its next
  export (the store is `v4`).
- **The emotions** (`face-acting/emotions.js`): the basic seven and the nuances an actor plays (amused, wry, skeptical,
  worried, embarrassed, determined, tender, pained, stifled, irritated, hopeful, smug, pensive, shocked), and
  `composeFace`: an intensity, a BLEND (the upper face from one emotion, the lower from another: bittersweet), a MASK (a
  shown emotion's mouth over a felt one that leaks through the brows and the eyes: the polite smile over worry), a lean
  to a side, and an eye look as the upper face.
- **The performer** (`face-acting/perform.js`): a performance in beats (a face from the emotions, an onset spontaneous or
  posed, a gaze, a state: listening, speaking, thinking, attentive; a brow flash; a micro-expression) becomes a take as
  a capture records it: each unit's curve at 60 fps, the gaze, and the events. The changes ease in and out over FACS's
  onsets and offsets, jittered per unit so none move in lockstep; the brows and the eyes lead the mouth by a little over
  a tenth of a second; a held expression lives (the moving hold); a micro-expression leaks for a fifth of a second; the
  blinks come at the state's rate (more speaking than attending), at a thought's close and with a large gaze shift,
  never through a brow flash; the eyes fixate, drift and jump on the main sequence, look away while thinking and glance
  off while speaking. Seeded: the same performance plays the same take; `captureFrame` reads a frame as a FACS state.
- **The take in the engine** (the hero door's `perform`, `relational-face-rig.js` `performanceTrack`, `scene-gltf.js`):
  a realistic hero's `perform: { <take>: a performance }` exports each take as a face-only clip, `face:<take>`, a LINEAR
  weights channel keyed at 30 fps that an engine layers over a body clip (the face's weights masked from it). The gaze
  plays on ARKit's look targets (`eyeLookUp/Down/In/Out`, each eye's globe turned 25° about its centre), so the eyes move
  with no bone; the jaw (a bone) is said apart. Refused by name on another head. `/hero-live` plays a take as a take of
  its own over the body's idle.
- **The globes in the face rig**: the one skin's globes were outside the rig, so the blink's sink behind the shut lid
  never applied (a speck of iris could show through a shut lid). They are in it now: still, but for the gaze's turn and
  the blink's sink.
- **Speech over the acting face** (`face-acting/speech.js`, a beat's `say`): a beat may speak a line (a text, `*word*`
  emphasized; or phonemes, ARPAbet or the IPA a speech engine writes, timed by their own audio where they carry times).
  The words become phonemes by rule (a short list of the words the rules get wrong first), the phonemes the fifteen
  visemes of the industry's lip-sync set, each holding the units it needs against its neighbours by its dominance
  (Cohen and Massaro's coarticulation: the lips round ahead of an oo, a vowel's jaw gives way); every m, b and p shut, the
  f and the v the lower lip under the teeth. `rate`, `articulation` (mumbled … enunciated), `jaw` and `lips`. The line
  lays its units over the face: a rounded lip draws the smile in, a pressed or tightened mouth lets go while it speaks,
  the brows and the eyes keep the emotion, an emphasized word lifts the brows, a sentence's close may take a blink.
- **The mouth's speech shapes** (`head-relational.js` `ACTIONS`): `pucker` (AU18), `funnel` (AU22), `rollUpper` and
  `rollLower` (AU28 by lip, `AU28T` and `AU28B`), `lipsPart` (AU25), each a morph target on the realistic face.
- **The jaw in a take** (`relational-face-rig.js` `jawOpen`): the jaw bone's own turn (25°, the clips' range end) as
  ARKit's `jawOpen` target over everything the bone moves, so a take or a capture opens the mouth with no bone and
  layers over any body clip; the clips still turn the bone. The face store is `v7`.
- **The realistic face's mouth, cleaner** (`hero-relational-head.js` `oneSkinFollow`): each lip carried by its own
  muscles about the mouth, so the lips part (carried by both, the upper and the lower moved as one); the nose held still
  by its own beads where an action leaves it; and the settle onto the moved skin kept to the eyes and the brows, where it
  was tuned: about the mouth and the nose it stood points out in spikes, the smile's and the frown's among them. The
  smile, the frown and every mouth target rebuild cleaner on the next export.
- **The mouth with teeth** (realistic laws 12, `hero-one-skin.js` `teeth`): a hero minted now has teeth. The bag behind
  the lips is cut open at its front into a cup facing in, and in it the head's own dentition, each crown a tube along its
  bead (the incisors blades that widen and thin to a flat edge, the cheek teeth shaded deeper in), the upper on the head
  bone and the lower and the tongue on the jaw's, so speech and an open mouth show teeth and a tongue where laws 11 showed
  the bag's dark front. And the mouth opens as an almond, not a box: shut, the lips' cut is one point either lip's, and
  bound wholly to its bone to the corner each side tore away along the whole cut; toward each corner both sides' share of
  the jaw now eases to a half, so the corners stay met and move half the jaw's way, down and back along its arc. A hero
  minted under laws 11 or before keeps its bag and its corners, byte for byte.

### The yoke: cloth on the tiered trunk hangs from the chest, not the shoulder

A jacket, a vest or a loose shirt on the tiered body read as a box over the chest: a shelf at the shoulders, its sides
falling straight past the armpit with the arms tucked under it. Measured on a person and on a beast-kin, the cause is
the trunk's top rings. On the tiered body they are the yoke: they run out into the shoulder balls (a person's at
x 0.348 m, the ball's centre at 0.335). A copy piece (`body-garment.js`) carried each ring out along its own normal, so
the yoke's side stood off sideways past the ball's outer edge (a person's jacket to 0.40 m, a brute beast-kin's 9 cm
past its shoulder). Its drape then held every ring below at least that far out, less a little per metre, so the side
fell from the shoulder point instead of from the chest.

- **The yoke** (`body-garment.js` `yokeOf`, `YOKE_SIDE`). On a trunk with shoulder balls, its rings above the armpit
  (the balls' lowest point) are the yoke. There the cloth stands out sideways by a quarter of its ease at most, so it
  lies on the shoulder with its armhole at the arm's root (a person's jacket at 0.36 m, the shoulder at 0.348). A yoke
  ring holds nothing out below it: the drape begins at the armpit, held by the chest, the bust and the shoulder
  blades. A body without shoulder balls (the classic body), and every piece off the trunk, is cut as before.

  Still open: a trunk piece's ease scales with the trunk's radius (`proportional`, against a limb's 0.1 m), so a very
  wide trunk (a hulking beast-kin) stands its cloth off by some 7 cm and can swallow the top of its arms.

### Home windows: a house wears a home's windows from its tradition, the steel grid kept for other buildings

A new house is stamped `houseLook: 2` (`polygonizer/floorplan-styles.js` HOME_WINDOWS): its windows are drawn from its
`design.tradition` and its style family, never the steel `crittall` grid of a workshop, which stays in the catalog for
the buildings that want it and for a house that names it. A house minted before keeps its windows, byte for byte.

- **North American**: double-hung, six-over-six, cottage, colonial, casement, picture and prairie, in the trim's paint
  or a modern black.
- **European** (`british`, `metric`): casement, German tilt-turn, transom, six-over-six and French, in the trim's paint,
  anthracite or a dark timber.
- **Asian** (`japanese`): the new `slider` (the hikichigai: two sashes sliding past each other, the meeting stiles side
  by side), and casement or picture, in aluminium.
- A home's glazing bars are slim, not the frame's own width.
- **Placed as an architect places them** (`polygonizer/home-windows.js`, `houseLook: 2`): each facade a grid of axes
  every storey keeps, so windows stack (void over void, solid over solid), 2 ft clear of the corners, the entry
  facade laid round the front door. Each room takes the axes its use asks: glazing to floor area by room (a living
  room ~15%, a bedroom ~11%), a bedroom a window it can be left by (a sash on a 2.5 ft sill, a fixed pane turned to a
  casement), a bathroom the standard window (smaller, over the fixtures, frosted), a kitchen over the counter, a hall
  on the facade lit, a store or laundry blind; a big room short of light a mulled pair on its axes.
- **A house knows its north** (`compass: { north, hemisphere }`), apart from the plan's N/S/E/W; absent, it orients
  itself, its living room's longest outside wall to the sun, and the day rooms take their windows sun side first.
- **The window laws** (`polygonizer/window-laws.js`), in the structure read as `windows`: daylight (the code's 8%),
  egress, blind service rooms, stacking, one head line a storey, corners, rhythm, and each facade's share of glass.

### Hostile non-human body: the beast-kin on the seventh generation

A beast-type humanoid foe (a bestiary skin `{ people: lupine | ursine | feline | draconic | avian | insectoid }` rolled
below the hero door) was built on the creature biped: the Pale Warden's ring plan, with a library head swapped onto its
neck stub. The undead left that body for the tiered hero; the beast-kin did not. Measured with the hero's own stretch
audit (walk, jog and sprint on the creature's vajra rig):
- the biped's knees pinch to 0.28–0.32 of their rest section in the sprint and twist up to 42°, where the tiered
  hero's knee bridge holds 0.76;
- its arm tubes push out of a box trunk that has no shoulders;
- fur and scale cards are half its triangles;
- the opt-in bridges (`style.drawn`) fold five faces at the forearm. They are the tiered body's bridges without its
  fold bones, hinge zones or sockets.

This theme freezes the biped as the sixth generation, and stands the beast-kin on the tiered body.

- **The sixth generation, held** (`egocube/creature-gen6.char.test.js`). The biped and its library heads stay as they
  are for every row minted on them. One sheet per procedure the biped runs is pinned byte for byte, its plan, its
  recipe and its mesh: digitigrade legs with a tail (designed and in its kit), plantigrade legs, wings on the arms, and a
  second pair of arms. Each sheet is found in code from the lineages' rolls, dressed as the cube dresses it. The
  creature-door undead's skull and gaunt face (`creature-heads/derive.js`) are named sixth-generation; the undead stand
  on the tiered body with their own.
- **A refined station's weights sum to one** (`station-loft-body.js` `extendBinds`). A station refined between two
  uneven neighbours blended its weights by u and rounded them without settling, missing 1 by a millionth. The bind
  then refused it, so a species bound to its skeleton and given `style.drawn` (a tail loft's stations) could not be
  rigged. The blend now settles whenever its rounding misses 1. A blend that already summed to 1 is untouched.
- **The stretch audit reads the body the door mints** (`scripts/hero-stretch.mjs`). The script built `heroRecord({ cast })`
  without the mint's default form, so it audited the deprecated classic body. It now stamps the tiered body;
  `--body classic` audits the other. The form slice (`--form`) reads its build as before. On the tiered body the knee's
  and the elbow's regions now count every ring of their bridge (`hero-stretch.js` `STRETCH_REGIONS`), where the limbs'
  own end rings stay rigid and read 1. A classic body has no bridges and reads as it did.
- **The beast card on the tiered body** (`lib/graph/beast/`). A hero takes `beast: { kin, legs?, fingers?, toes?, claws?,
  tail?, wings?, arms?, head?, cover?, expression? }`.
  The kin is a card (`beast/cards.js`) of words, never geometry:
  - `reads`: what the kin reads as;
  - `fingers`: 3 or 4, the thumb among them; `toes`: 3, 4 or 5; `tail`: the tail it carries;
  - `claws`: none, blunt or long, and their tone;
  - `mass`: each part family's girth against a person's, and the waist on top of the trunk (over 1 a barrel, under 1
    a wasp's waist);
  - `rest`: the hunch, the knees and the arms' hang.

  The door records the card's words under the spec's own, as the undead's are, so an edit reaches them (`beastWords`):
  - bald, the body bare in one coat (its lineage's first swatch unless the palette names a skin), the feet bare;
  - the rest as the hero's gesture, the idle breathing in it, the walk tilted by the hunch.

  The girths go on the hero's plan before the tiered passes (`beastFlesh`), so the bridges, the shoulder's ball, web
  and cone are built on the body as it now is. The waist's swell is centred on the torso's narrowest section, fading up
  the chest and to nothing by the hip joint. A barrel's depth goes forward (its back held), so the seat still stands
  behind the lower back; a pinch draws in all round. After the tiered passes (`beastHands`):
  - the hand keeps the card's fingers. The outer ones go from the skin and the dials, and the rig stays whole, so every
    clip plays.
  - a hooked claw comes out of each kept digit's tip and each toe's. It is a four-station loft that curls toward the
    palm or the floor, riding the digit's last bone.

  The legs are the hero's word, not the kin's (a lineage stands digitigrade by how far from a person its sheet rolled).
  Refused: an unknown kin or word, a beast off the tiered body, and a beast that is undead too. A hero without `beast`
  is unchanged.

  Machine gate (`beast/tiered.test.js`):
  - the words recorded, the operator's own over them;
  - a barrel's waist swelling past its chest, its back held and its centre forward; a wasp's waist pinching inside it;
  - the forearm at the card's girth, and the shoulder's ball on the thicker arm;
  - three fingers kept with the rig whole and the dials pruned;
  - a claw past each digit's tip on its last bone, long ones longer than blunt, none on a clawless kin;
  - the bind and the rig audit clean;
  - refusals;
  - the stretch audit through walk, jog and sprint. The barrel kin on the brute build pinches above 0.7 and no worse
    than the brute hero, and folds no more.

  The audit over each kin (8 phases a gait), against the creature biped's sprint knee of 0.28–0.32:
  - bear-kin on the brute: 0.81;
  - insect-kin on the lithe: 0.72;
  - wolf-kin: 0.76;
  - dragon-kin on the heroic: 0.80.

  Minted through `create_character`, the male kin draw no core advisory. A female barrel kin is told its waist is as
  wide as its hips, which is the barrel's read. Eyes: front, side and the gaits, cropped to the hand and the foot.
  Eyes gate: the operator's to judge.
- **Digitigrade legs on the tiered body** (`beast/legs.js`, `beast.legs: 'digitigrade'`). The rig's leg is already a
  digitigrade chain (hip, knee, hock, toes; a person's hock is the ankle on the floor), so a digitigrade kin is the same
  chain with its joints moved and the parts below the knee made for them:
  - the joints are shares of the hip's height, taken from the creature biped's digitigrade template: the knee forward,
    the hock raised and back, the toes' base on the floor ahead of it;
  - the thigh is turned and stretched about the hip onto its new line, each station's offset from the line kept, and
    the hip's socket fold follows it;
  - the foot is a metatarsus from the hock to the toes' base, with a pad under the ball and the card's toes splayed
    ahead (the middle ones: no big toe), each with its claw on the toes' bone;
  - the hock is bridged as the knee is (`tiered-form.js` `TIERED_HOCK`): the shank and the metatarsus stop short of
    it, a bridge spans it, and its rings ride a fold pushed to the heel's side (the knee's goes to its front, since the
    two bend opposite ways). A chain splits as one unit with its hock (`bridgedChains`); a person's ankle names no hock
    bridge and is untouched.

  A plantigrade kin keeps a person's foot, with the card's toes (the big toe among them, the outer ones gone from the
  skin and the dials). A digitigrade kin's knee rests bent some 75°, so a person's stance bend and swing fold, added to
  it, folded the knee's bridge shut: a jog's 115° swing tuck left its ring at 0.12 of its rest. A digitigrade kin's
  gaits draw them in (`DIGITIGRADE_GAIT`: the walk's lift 26°, a run's tuck 50°, no stance bend), on every walk and run
  it carries, with the operator's own dials over them. A paw on a raised hock takes nothing cut for a person's foot: a
  footwear word (a shoe was drawn over the metatarsus) and an armour build (its sabatons refused the paw's missing toes
  by a part's name) are refused on a digitigrade kin, saying so.

  Machine gate (`beast/legs.test.js`):
  - the joints, the turned thigh and its socket's line;
  - the hock's bridge on its fold to the heel's side, its bone in the rig;
  - the metatarsus, the pad and the kept toes with their claws, the dials naming them;
  - a plantigrade foot with the card's toes;
  - footwear and an armour build refused on a paw, allowed on a plantigrade foot;
  - the gait dials, the operator's over them;
  - the rig audit, with the planted toes where they stand;
  - the stretch audit through the kin's own walk, jog and sprint: worst pinch above 0.7, no more folds than a person's,
    twist under 30°;
  - a person's jog on the same knee pinching under 0.4, the case the gait dials are for.

  Measured: the wolf-kin walks, jogs and sprints at a worst pinch of 0.87 (its knee 0.97), where the plain hero's own
  sprint pinches its unbridged ankle to 0.45. The wolf-kin, the bird-kin and the dragon-kin mint through
  `create_character` with no core advisory. Eyes: front, side and the gaits. Eyes gate: the operator's to judge.
- **The generic socket** (`beast/socket.js` `rootWeb`). Where a limb leaves a trunk that has no ring of its own to meet,
  a fillet of skin runs from inside the trunk's section to the limb's own ring and ends on that ring point for point, so
  the two weld into one surface. It is the shoulder web's principle with nothing of the human in it: the trunk, the
  limb, the ring and the bones are named by the caller.
  - The base ring is the limb's ring, spread wide and sunk back along the limb's axis, each point held inside the
    trunk's section at its height (`tiered-form.js` `torsoSection`, which now takes the trunk's name).
  - The rings between are eased in and swelled a little.
  - Its skin hands the trunk's bone to the limb's over its length, never at once.

  The hero's shoulder keeps its own web, ball and cone, byte for byte.
- **What the frame adds** (`beast/topology.js`): the egocube's topology, carried from the creature biped onto the
  hero's own body.
  - **The tail** (`beast.tail`: thin, thick, brush or stub, the biped's `TAILS`; its default is the kin's card's: the
    wolf-kin's brush, the cat-kin's thin, the dragon-kin's thick, the bear-kin's stub). It is a loft from the back of
    the pelvis at the hip's height, its joints the carriage's scaled to the hero. Each station is half and half between
    the tail's bones at its joint. The bones ride the pelvis: no clip poses a tail yet, so every clip plays.
  - **The tail's socket** ends on the tail's first ring. The tail swells past that ring, so a socket ending further out
    ran under the swell and showed it through as a slit.
  - **The arm-wings** (`beast.wings: 'arms'`): the biped's five flight feathers, flat vanes trailing down and back from
    the hand and the forearm, set on the hero's own elbow and knuckles and riding those bones, toned a shade either side
    of the coat.
  - **The second arms** (`beast.arms: 4`): a smaller pair under the first, folded forward. Each has an upper arm on the
    torso's side, a forearm and a mitten hand. The elbow and the wrist are bridged as the hero's are, with no fold since
    their bend is held, and the shoulder is welded to the torso by the generic socket. Their joints ride the torso.

  Machine gate (`beast/topology.test.js`):
  - the tail behind the hips at their height, its bones on the pelvis;
  - its socket ending on its first ring point for point, its base held inside the pelvis, its skin handing over
    monotonically;
  - the tail word over the card's;
  - five vanes a side on the forearm and the hand;
  - the second arms below the first and folded forward, bridged and welded, their joints on the torso, in the dials;
  - with all three, the bind and the rig audit clean, and the walk's worst pinch and folds those of the same body
    without them;
  - refusals.

  Eyes: the wolf-kin's tail before and after the socket's fix, the bird-kin's wings and the insect-kin's four arms
  through the gaits, cropped to each socket. Eyes gate: the operator's to judge.
- **The beast head on the tiered neck** (`beast/head.js`, `beast.head`). A beast-kin wears its kin's library head by
  default (`creature-heads`: the bear's, the wolf's, the felid, the dragon's, the beaked, the mandibled). The head is
  dressed for its coat by the creature door's own steps, now one shared helper (`egocube/plan.js` `libraryHead`: the
  skin's tones, the people's eye accent, scaled to the body); the sixth-generation pins hold through the move.
  - It is seated by its nape on the hero's head base. Its skull rides the head bone; its jaw is a bone of its own,
    hinged at the head's pivot and opened by the rig's jaw chain (a clip key's `jaw`). The rig's head top sits on the
    skull's crown, and the blank trunk's head is taken off.
  - The record's head is `none` (no hair or face words). `beast.head` names another library head, or `person` to keep
    a person's (bald) head. A beast's head under a person's head word is refused.
  - **The neck leans forward under it** (`NECK_LEAN`, 26°, its length kept). The library heads are drawn for the
    creature biped's neck, which runs 27° forward into the back of the skull. On a person's upright neck the skull sat
    forward of it, and its back rim crossed the neck's back as a saw-toothed edge.
  - **The nape** is a fillet from the neck's middle ring, point for point, flaring past the head's base into the skull,
    its top ring buried there. Each ring is the neck's own top ring scaled, so its slots never twist, and its skin hands
    the neck to the head over its length. The plan's own seam still seals the neck's end inside the head.

  Machine gate (`beast/head.test.js`):
  - the library head on the head base, its bones and the jaw chain, the blank head off;
  - the neck's lean and length;
  - the nape welded to the neck's ring, its top ring inside the compiled skull, its skin handing over;
  - the bind and the rig audit clean, and the jaw opened by the chain;
  - another library head, a person's head, and the refusals.

  All six kin mint through `create_character` with no core advisory. Eyes: the six heads through the gaits, the nape
  from the side and behind before and after the lean. The library head's own back rows still show a little of their
  low-poly rim from behind. Eyes gate: the operator's to judge.
- **Cover as form, not cards** (`beast/cover.js`, `beast.cover`: none, fur, scales, chitin or feathers; its default the
  kin's: fur for the bear-, wolf- and cat-kin, scales for the dragon-kin, feathers for the bird-kin, chitin for the
  insect-kin). The sixth generation built a coat as cards, half the biped's triangles. The seventh carries it as a
  material an engine lights.
  - **The tile.** Each kind is a tileable relief: a height field in metres on a 128-texel square, deterministic on its
    kind. Fur is strands lying down the body; scales and feathers are shingles in offset rows, each over the row above,
    a feather's vane narrowing to its tip; chitin is plates with grooves at their joints.
  - **The maps.** The form render's material reads the relief (`form/relief-material.js`) into glTF's maps: a base grey
    the vertex colour multiplies (the coat, darker in its hollows), the tangent-space normal, occlusion and roughness in
    one ORM image, and the height.
  - **The flat patch.** A flat patch at the tile's origin is level, white and unoccluded. A face the cover does not
    reach (the head, the claws, the eyes) samples it, so one material serves the whole figure.
  - **The mapping** (`coverMap`). The coat (a beast is bare, so its skin and the groups its clothes would be, its head
    excepted) is mapped by each part's own rings. The tile's u is a slot's place round them, a whole number of tiles so
    the wrap is seamless; its v is a station's arc length along their centres, so a curved tail, a flaring socket and the
    shoulder's funnel map as they run. A first mapping about one straight axis per part swung the tile round them. A cap's
    point takes its face's way round, and each corner's tangent is built the MikkTSpace way.
  - **The export.** It rides the lit skinned GLB (`export_model { skinned: true, lit: true }`). A beast-kin is now lit by
    the engine as the realistic body is: its corners carry their shading normals and no baked shade
    (`world-kinds.js`). The rig pack carries the cover only when asked (`packLayeredRig` `cover`): each corner's place
    on the tile and its tangent, and the maps (`coverTex`). The writer (`scene-gltf.js` `coverMaterial`) makes the
    figure's material from them: the base and the normal, the ORM image as occlusion and metallic-roughness (roughness
    factor 1, metal 0), the height in the material's extras (`mojulo.height`, with the tile and the depth) for an engine
    that reads parallax or displacement. glTF's default sampler repeats the tile. Absent, every pack and every file is
    byte for byte as before.
  - **The head's tufts.** Under a cover, the library head's details are spent by what reads at the hero's target, the
    drawn creature's rule (`creature-drawn.js` `headAtTier`, its eyes as drawn): a tuft too short to break the outline is
    the material's, not a card.
  - **The page.** The World page draws the cover as paint, the coat's colour (its fills are unlit), until it lights a
    figure live.

  Machine gate (`beast/cover.test.js`; `export-model.beast.test.js`, on the E2E list):
  - each tile seamless at its edges, within its depth, deterministic, its flat patch level and white;
  - a hollow occluded more than a crest;
  - the coat mapped by its rings: the head and the claws on the flat patch, every tangent unit and square to its
    normal, no face taken the long way round the wrap;
  - the pack byte for byte without a cover, and no cover carried unlit;
  - the kin's cover, the operator's word over it, and fewer head tufts under it;
  - minted and exported, the GLB's skinned mesh carrying TEXCOORD_0, NORMAL and TANGENT, and a material with the four
    maps, a zero metal factor, the extras and the walk;
  - with `cover: 'none'`, none of them.

  Eyes: the four tiles' maps side by side, and the wolf-kin with its fur and without, lit by three.js in the hero-live
  viewer (`/hero-live`, the same GLB an engine gets). The fur's relief reads on the body, and the head drops its tuft
  cards (8,812 triangles to 7,096). Eyes gate: the operator's to judge.
- **The route: new beast-kin mint on the seventh generation** (`egocube/plan.js` `beastOnTiered`, `planFromSheet`). A
  sheet below the hero door of a kin the beast cards know is now the hero door's call, `create { as: 'hero' }`, with
  the beast's words read from the sheet:
  - the kin is its ancestry; the legs are digitigrade when the sheet derives them;
  - the fingers, claws, tail and cover come from its lineage's cues as its humanity gates them, and feathers for the
    bird-kin;
  - the frame's wings ride the arms and its second pair of arms is the beast's;
  - the library head is its people's, and the face's derives become its expression (`beast.expression`: each control
    in −1 … 1, read by the library head);
  - its build is the hero's tune and its height its stature, within the tune's range.

  A designed sheet person enough to wear the cut (`CLOTHED_H`) wears it as the hero's outfit. One below it goes bare:
  its adornment is not worn on the tiered body yet, and the ledger says so, as it says where every other note landed or
  what is pending. A people of the operator's own with no card, a sheet with its own form, and any call that asks for
  `gen: 6` stay on the creature biped. Rows already minted are stored as minted, so they keep their body.

  The bestiary follows. A foe skinned `{ people: lupine }` and a cast's beast-kin play a person's moves from the
  library on the field (`gameworld/casting.js` `fieldOf`), not the creature loop's walk and jog. The fight game's
  roster fields a beast-kin, where it refused one below the hero door (`gameworld/runner.js`).

  Machine gate (`beast/route.test.js`):
  - each kin's sheet routed with its words, a valid hero spec, and a ledger row at or pending for every note;
  - both leg procedures reached;
  - the wings and the second arms carried, and the ledger saying where;
  - `gen: 6` and a lineage with no card on the biped;
  - clothed and bare by `CLOTHED_H`, the ledger naming the bare one's adornment;
  - the call compiling, deterministic;
  - the expression reaching the library head, and a control outside −1 … 1 refused.

  The egocube's own tests read the sixth generation through `gen: 6`, and its pins hold byte for byte. The foes' and the
  fight game's tests read the new field.

- **A silhouette per kin, not six slim swimmers** (`beast/cards.js`, `beast/tiered.js`). On the tiered body every kin
  read as one lean figure in six coats, where the creature biped's had read hulking. Three things kept it lean:
  - the route stood a kin on the canonical frame under a person's light build tune;
  - the cards' mass was girth alone, and timid;
  - nothing gave the upper back or the chest's front a mass of its own.

  Now:
  - **The build is the tiered body's own.** The route passes the sheet's build as the cast's build form
    (`cast: { pole, build }`, HERO_BUILDS), so a brute bear-kin stands on the brute's chest and arms; a child keeps the
    pole's cast. The rolled build varies a kin within its type.
  - **A frame per kin.** Each card names its proportions as tune words (`frame`: shoulders, depth, legs, neck, waist,
    hips), recorded under the operator's own tune (`beastWords`). A tune given as a move or a list stands as given.
  - **Three masses of the trunk's own.** `hump` (the back under the neck swelling out behind, its front held), `keel`
    (the chest's front swelling forward, from the throat to the belly, its back held) and `mass.hips` (the pelvis and
    the belly over it). The hump sits at the neck's root: one at the shoulder blades folded the back in a sprint, the
    swinging arm's cone driven into it.
  - **Bolder girths.** The digitigrade metatarsus is heavier (`legs.js` `META`), so a raised foot no longer reads as
    a stilt.

  Each kin is now its own silhouette: the bear the heavyweight (a barrel, a hump, short legs), the dragon the hulking
  V (broad and deep, thick haunches), the wolf the brawler (an inverted triangle), the cat the athlete (the one lean
  kin, strong haunches), the bird top-heavy on its keel, the insect segmented (a broad thorax, a wasp's waist, full
  hips).

  The nape fillet's crown is now sized to the skull whatever the neck's girth (`beast/head.js`). A neck thicker than
  1.5 of a person's stood its crown out through the back of the skull.

  Machine gate (`beast/tiered.test.js`, `route.test.js`):
  - the frame recorded under the operator's tune;
  - the hump, the keel and the hips each moving its own side and holding the other;
  - the route's build in the cast;
  - the stretch audit as before: worst pinch 0.86–0.88 on the digitigrade kin's own gaits. The plantigrade kin read
    0.52–0.55 at the unbridged ankle, as they did before this.

  Eyes: the six kin on two builds each, front and side mid-stride. Eyes gate: the operator's to judge.

- **Detail as form** (`beast/detail.js`; `beast.ridge`, `beast.ruff`, `beast.abdomen`). The silhouette's breakers are
  real parts again. The creature biped drew them as cards, and the cover material cannot break an outline.
  - **The ridge** (`ridge: 'spines'`, the dragon-kin's by default). A crest of flat spines, thin across and wide
    along. It runs up the neck's back, down the back's centre from the neck's root to the hips, and down the tail's
    top. The spines are tallest over the shoulders, each raked toward the tail and riding the bone it stands on (the
    neck, the torso, the lumbar, the pelvis, the tail's own). A small spine stays a blade: its thickness is at most a
    third of its width.
  - **The ruff** (`ruff: 'ruff'`). Two staggered rows of heavy tufts round the back and the sides of the neck's root,
    hanging out and down, mirrored, riding the torso. The route sets it where the sheet's fur cue names a ruff: the
    wolf-kin's, and the bear-kin's long shoulder fur.
  - **The abdomen** (`abdomen: 'gaster'`, the insect-kin's by default). A full ovoid out of the back of the pelvis,
    carried back and down, a shape of the tail's on its bones and socket. A kin carries a tail or an abdomen, never
    both: the door refuses the two together.
  - **The coverts.** A shorter row of feathers laid over the arm-wings' flights. The wing still reads as a comb of
    flights rather than one feathered surface; a broad vane is not built yet.

  The route reads the dragon's silhouette pick: the crest gives spines; a frill or folded wings gives none, and
  those stay pending in the ledger. The ledger names `spec.beast.ridge` and `spec.beast.ruff` where they land.

  Machine gate (`beast/detail.test.js`, `route.test.js`):
  - the spines on the midline, flat, raked, in order down the back, each on the bone at its height;
  - the tufts at the neck's root, round the back and the sides, hanging, mirrored;
  - the abdomen full in its middle and behind, and the tail-and-abdomen refusal;
  - `none` taking each away, an unknown word refused;
  - the rig whole with every detail on;
  - the route's ruff and crest from the sheet.

  Eyes: the dragon, the wolf, the bear, the insect and the bird, walking and sprinting. Eyes gate: the operator's to
  judge.

- **The snake-kin: a lamia on a serpent's coil** (`beast/serpent.js`, `beast.legs: 'serpent'`, the `serpentine` kin
  and lineage). A person's torso, arms and head on the tiered body, carried upright on a serpent's coil in place of the
  legs.
  - **One surface.** The legs' parts go (the thigh, the shank, the foot, the toes, the knee's bridge); their bones and
    joints stay, so every clip still plays, moving nothing seen. The pelvis is cut at the hip ring, and the coil grows
    out of that ring point for point, as the nape grows out of the neck: no crossing to crease. It runs down and a
    little forward to the ground under the hips, then along the ground behind in an S, tapering to a point. Its rings
    are the hip ring's slots carried down the path by a frame that never twists, rounded through every bend, each at
    its half width and height, so on the ground its underside lies on the floor.
  - **Planted.** Its first joint rides the pelvis; the rest are planted (`rig.planted`, new: joints that ride nothing
    and stand where they rest in every pose). The length on the ground lies there whatever the hips do. A rig without
    them is unchanged.
  - **The slither.** Each link on the ground is a chain about the vertical, turning every joint after it. The rig
    carries the wave they make (`rig.wave`, new: its chains, its amplitude, its wavelength in links). Every gait's clip
    plays it at its phase, travelling toward the tail (`hero-motion.js` `locomotionClips`, `station-loft-rig.js`
    `waveAt`). A rig without one plays its clips as before.
  - **Its gaits** (`SERPENT_GAIT`). A person's run lowered and drove the hips (its knee's bend, its flight, its lean,
    a long stride's vault), which squeezed the coil's upright length into a kink. A coil's gaits hold the hips at
    their height, and its run's stride is half a sprinter's.
  - **The kin** (`beast/cards.js` `serpentine`). Five fingers, no claws, a person's head with its hair kept (a card's
    `hair`). Its coat colours its own groups only (a card's `coat`: the coil and the hips over it); the torso keeps a
    person's skin, bare as every kin is. Its cover is scales on those groups alone (`cover.js` `beastCoatOf`, a
    `coverMap` group list).
  - **The door.** It refuses what is cut for legs: trousers, footwear, an armour build.
  - **The lineage** (`egocube/ancestry.js` `serpentine`, its derive `legs = serpent`). A sheet of it routes to the
    tiered body with the coil, five fingers and scales. A blind roll picks only a human ancestry, so no stored sheet
    moves. The bestiary's people skins take it: a foe `{ people: 'serpentine' }`. The ledger is honest about the face:
    the cheek and spine scales, the slit pupils and the stare are pending on a person's head. A person-headed kin's
    sheet sets no expression it would not read.

  Machine gate (`beast/serpent.test.js`, `route.test.js`):
  - the coil's first ring the pelvis's hip ring, point for point; the legs' parts gone and their bones kept;
  - its underside on the floor, and every planted joint at its height through the walk and the sprint;
  - the wave's peak travelling one link a wavelength toward the tail;
  - a hero without a coil carrying no wave and no planted joint, and the rig refusing an unknown chain or a planted
    core joint;
  - the bind and the rig audit clean;
  - the stretch audit through its own walk and sprint (worst pinch 0.82–0.86, no more folds than a person's);
  - the scales on the coil and the hips only, the top bare;
  - the door's refusals;
  - the route's coil from the derive.

  Eyes: the lamia front, side and from above, at two phases of the walk and mid-sprint; the S on the ground swings
  between them. Eyes gate: the operator's to judge. Not yet: a snake's head, slit pupils and scaled cheeks on a

- **Each sheet its own beast: the creature-from-sheet flow on the seventh generation** (`creature-heads/derive.js`,

  - **The serpent skull** (`HEAD_DERIVATIONS.serpent`). Drawn from the wolf by row moves: a flat crown, wide at the

    the skull's edge, the forked tongue, no ears and no teeth. It serves the snake-kin, so the lamia is the
    snake-headed lady. The dragon, the nearer skull, is drawn in metres where it sits: the row moves scale heights
    about the origin, so they pulled its crown down from two metres while its snout stayed up.
  - **A designed head** (`beast.head: { from, moves?, eye?, regions?, ornaments?, palette? }`). A head drawn from a

  - **A coil is dressed above its hips.** A clothed snake-kin wears the top hemmed at the waist and its upper pieces.

- **The people composer: principles of creation, not races** (`beast/cards.js`, `beast/tiered.js`, `beast/lexicon.js`,

### House forms: a townhouse and a modern block beside the detached house

A house carries `form: 'detached' | 'townhouse' | 'block'` (`polygonizer/house-forms.js`), beside its size (`tier`) and
its finish (`style`); absent, the detached house the generator always drew. A form plans every storey as it is lived
in, in the house kernel's own plan contract, so the stack, the stair, the windows and the read build it as any house.

- **Townhouse**: narrow and deep, three or four storeys; the stair hall along a party wall holds a straight flight
  and a passage beside its well, the same zone on every floor; the rooms stacked front to back: kitchen and dining to
  the garden (a glazed door at the end of the kitchen's back wall), the living room to the street, bedrooms and baths
  above. `attached: 'both'` by default (mid-terrace); `'left'` / `'right'` an end unit. Party walls take no window.
- **Block**: the modern block, compact and near square, two or three storeys, a hall down its middle holding the
  stair, rooms either side; an open living floor below.
- **Windows** (`houseLook: 2`): a narrow facade is laid from its plan (the stair hall's bay, the door below and the
  window over it; a main room's two bays), a townhouse's sashes tall on a low sill; a tall storey (a block's) raises
  the window head with its ceiling and a block aims for more light; a glazed garden door lights its room.
- **The draw** gives a form its own storeys and footprint (a townhouse three or four on a narrow deep lot, a block two
  or three on a compact one) and lets it plan its own front door; a footprint that cannot hold its stair or its rooms
  is refused at mint, naming the size it needs. No new tool or kind: one knob on `mint_building`'s recipe.

### A house that names its width keeps its stair inside

A house whose recipe names its `width` and has stairs (every two-storey house the new-house draw stamps) took the
house's width for its stair's: `placeStairs` read the stair's width from the options the house rides in, so the flight
was laid as wide as the house and its well cut through the slab above, most of it outside the walls. The stair now
takes its own width (its spec's, else the stair default). Such a house renders with its stair inside, at its width; a
house that never named its width is unchanged.

### Townhouse traditions: contemporary brownstone, London terrace, Dutch canal and Japanese small houses

The house library grows by four contemporary street-house traditions, each a style family (`floorplan-styles.js`),
a roofline (`architecture/roof.js`), its home windows per region and its furniture language (`furnishings/languages.js`):

- **brownstone** (North American rowhouse): coursed brown sandstone, a flat roof behind a deep projecting cornice
  (`roof: 'cornice'`), tall sashes, a dark lacquered door; parlour walnut, velvet and bouclé.
- **terrace** (London): yellow-grey stock brick or white stucco, slate with its ridge parallel to the street and its
  gables on the party walls (`roof: 'terrace-slate'`), six-over-six and two-over-two sashes, a navy, green or black
  door; roll arms, linen and tartan.
- **canal** (Dutch canal and infill houses): dark manganese or warm brick, a steep gable flush to the street
  (`roof: 'canal-gable'`) or a flat roof, tall tilt-turn and French windows in anthracite; low, spare, pale oak.
- **kyosho** (the Japanese small house): white render, charred cedar boards or corrugated galvalume, a galvalume
  mono-pitch (`roof: 'galvalume-shed'`) or a flat roof, aluminium sliders; hinoki floors, low and plain.

New facades: `facadeStyle: 'stone'` (coursed ashlar), `'render'` (smooth stucco at any storey height) and `'boards'`
(vertical timber on an open joint, charred cedar by default). A gable roof takes `ridge: 'short'` to turn its ridge
across the long way. A house of `houseLook: 2` rolls its family from its `form` and `design.tradition` (a townhouse
its tradition's street house, a block a modern one, a Japanese house kyosho); a house of the first look rolls from
the first five families, as always.

A home's gables (`houseLook: 2`, `polygonizer/gable-skin.js`) are the wall below carried up, not a flat roof tint: brick
and stone continue their bond from the top storey, render is one plane, boards and siding run to the rake, and each roof
finishes the edge its own way: a terrace's party walls rise through the slates as coped parapets with a chimney stack and
its pots at the ridge, a canal house's street gable is coped, with a loft window under a hoist beam, and every other
gable takes a verge band (a masonry coping or the trim's barge board). The first look keeps the roof's flat gable.

### Merge fixes: the seams the 10/25 to 10/28 merges left open

An audit of the four days of merges onto `1026-consolidated` found these; each is fixed with a test that fails without
it.

- **A race reaches GLB and the engine packs.** A racer or supercar minted now is drawn in the form render, its parts
  packed `{ form: { o, s, n, q, nrm, col, idx, groups, mats } }` (`vehicle-rig.js` `packFormMesh`). The rig export read
  every part as a painted one and threw on its colours, so any engine pack of a race (`clips: '_all'`) crashed and a
  plain GLB left the cars out. `scene-gltf.js` `decodeRigPart` reads the form mesh one level down: the same quantized
  positions and linear colours. Its material slots and normals stay the page's; a GLB carries the albedo.
- **A genre level in a building routes to `design_game`.** The `game` routing card and three fixture rows sent "a
  stealth level through an office" to a `create_game` argument that does not exist. The building level is
  `design_game`'s (`quick.building`, or a world level's `building`; card `game-building`): the phrasing moves to the
  `game-design` card, and the rows expect `design_game` in its quick mode.
- **The realistic hero keeps the door's hair and expression.** The record stored `hair` and `expression` only for the
  landmark and anime heads, so on the realistic body (the relational head) both were dropped without a word: every
  realistic crew wore its rolled ancestry's cut and a neutral face, and the pack-v2 wavy fall never landed there. The
  record now reads the landmark hair as the face's `scalp` (`layered.js` `scalpOfHair`: the same name where both
  libraries have one, the nearest cut where not, the `wave` as the curl), unless the face names its own, and stores the
  expression the relational face rig already reads. An explicit `head: 'relational'` takes both. Absent, nothing.
- **The roof a metal sheet is judged by is the one the render draws.** The mint rolled a house's family at look 1, the
  render at the house's look, tradition and form, so a townhouse or a block could be refused a sheet its roof would wear,
  or granted one its flat deck then dropped. Both read `floorplan-styles.js` `homeLook`.
- **`update_sketch` holds a house to the mint's gate.** An edit ran none of the mint's house checks and never re-derived
  the game/show purpose. The mint's block is `sketch-mint.js` `houseGate`, called at both: on an update a stamp fills
  only what the stored row carried, so a row minted before a stamp keeps its bytes; a purpose the row's level derived is
  derived again (a level added makes the house a game's), and a purpose the edit names stands.
- **A wide stair keeps to its zone.** The flight takes its own width since the stair-width fix, but the zone kept for it
  was still sized by the default, so a wide flight spilled out of a program house's zone and through a townhouse's party
  wall. The zone, a form's hall and the mint's footprint check take the widest flight asked for (`house-forms.js`
  `stairWidthOf`, `floorplan-structure.js` `stairSpanOf`). A house that names no wider flight is planned as before.
- **The table RPG export never fetches a browser, by construction.** The portrait shoot runs inside
  `withoutChromiumFetch`, so a caller's consent to the download no longer reaches it.
- **No plan citations from the seats and live-light work.** Sixteen comments cited plan files; three sat inside the
  controllable rules every World page serializes, so the sixteen controllable fixtures in `emit-channels.char.test.js`
  are re-pinned (three comment lines, nothing else).
- **The lockfile is back in step with `package.json`.** `npm ci` refused it (it lacked `esbuild-wasm`, listed `sharp`
  among the regular dependencies, and recorded the old Node floor).

Machine gate: the new and touched tests, then `npm run test:changed --since 1026-consolidated`. Eyes gate not run: no
one has looked at an exported race in an engine, a realistic crew's hair, or a wide stair in a townhouse.

### The realistic hair as its main shapes

The realistic hero's hair, re-cut for the seventh-generation look: a designed mass that gives a hero its outline, in one
colour, with nothing to fight the light. Its register is a dial between a realistic game's hair and a stylised one's.
The eyes gate is the operator's.

- **Hair as its main shapes** (realistic laws 10, `REALISTIC_LAWS_VERSION`; `epidermis/hair-locks.js` `lockHair`).
  Laws 7 to 9 grew a lawn of thousands of blades, banded root to tip with grey flecks. Under real light the bands read as
  noise, and a dark-brown groom greying a little came out silver. The alpha cards shimmered at their edges, the cap
  showed through as dark squares, and the outline was fuzzy. Now a stroke budget (the operator's: a number of major
  flows, volumized, and some trailers, that's it):
  - MAJOR FLOWS: the groom's guides (`dermal-hair.js` `growScalp`) gathered into a few dozen flows, by their roots,
    middles and ends, never across the part. Each flow's section is drawn through its own guides across it: a smooth
    arc fitted to them, so a broad flow lies on the head as its guides do. It is domed and grooved on top, flat beneath.
    Its root runs to the hairline and its end to the cut's line. Under it the cap is kept as a solid inner shell.
  - THE FLOWS LIE ON THE HEAD (`LOCK_CONFORM`). Over the scalp a flow's section wraps round the head at its spine's own
    height, not as a chord across it, and the higher a flow is rooted the further out it lies (the crown's hair over the
    nape's). Its root comes out of the scalp, and a root reached back off a curved crown is laid back on it. So the flows
    shingle, never planks standing off the head at angles (long hair at `stylize` 0 read as crumpled paper).
  - VOLUME: round by round, only the flows nearest where the scalp shows grow wider, and only over the scalp, until the
    overlap principle holds (below): widening every flow hung panels below the head.
  - TRAILERS: a few strokes per flow riding its edges toward its tip and on past a free tip, breaking its outline, never
    flaring off the mass along a guide of their own.
  - THE FADE: the shell's edge is smoothed into a curve (`hair-depict.js` `capMesh` `smoothEdge`, laws 10 only) and
    fringed with strand cards running out over the skin, so no hairline is a hard line. The fade is the hairline's only
    cards (a card as wide as a flow stood off the temples as a barred plank in the skinned GLB).
  - TIP CARDS (`LOCK_TIP`, toward `stylize` 0): laid on a lock's top as narrow cards side by side, each through the
    lock's own section, so a broad flow's cards curve with it; one straight card across a broad flow (up to 18 cm) stood
    off it.
  - One procedure per hair class (`lockClass`). Cropped is the shell alone, raised to the hair's length. Standing coils
    (an afro, a crop of curls) are a sculpted volume: the shell raised to where the coils stand, in puffs. Curly hair that
    falls (`curls`) is flows, as long hair is: as a volume it flared off one side of the head as a brim. Short and long
    hair are flows and trailers. Standing hair is anime sections: a lying layer of flows with laid-down spikes over it,
    less spiky than anime. Tied
    hair is flat flows pulled to the tie, with the tail (a ponytail, a braid, a bun) a separate mass: a core wrapped by
    locks. Locs and rows are ropes, each round with a twist groove, drawn in enough stations for its twist (`LOCK_ROPE`;
    fewer drew a braid as a flat zigzag).
  - Every stroke lies off the head's skin and ears and over the shell. A long flow also falls outside the hero's neck,
    shoulders and back (the compiled parts, `HAIR_HANG`). Its points below the head ride the neck and the torso
    (`boneWeights`), so the skinned GLB swings it with the body.
  - ONE colour, `Hair`: the hair as the eye averages it, so grey is a lighter whole, never flecks. `HairStreak` appears
    only where the groom asks for a streak. The cards draw the strand page undyed (`strands: 'plain'`), in the mass's
    colour.
  - THE FACE'S HAIR in the same register (`lockStrands`; `stylize` the face's, as the scalp's), each in one colour,
    with no root band:
    - A BEARD is its coat sculpted to where its hairs stand (`beardShell`, the coil's procedure), lumped finer at 0 and
      chunkier at 1. A short beard is that coat alone. Only hair whose tip leaves the skin, a full beard's chin, hangs
      as flows, rooted inside the coat so they come out at its edge. The coat is smoothed whole and then split at the
      lip line, so the jaw's half and the head's meet (smoothing each half pulled the seam open).
    - A MOUSTACHE's halves and each BROW are a band (`browMass`): one flat mass along it, its head rounded and its tail
      drawn in, with the dial's few strokes laid on it and held inside it: never a brow of two-tone blades, never a
      beard of small locks reading as scales.
    - A card face pushed off the skin onto itself is dropped (a fade card at the forehead had no area), and a tip card
      is never narrower than `LOCK_TIP.half`.
  - CLIPPED HAIR (`dermal-map.js` `CLIPPER`): hair a clipper takes under 4 mm (clipper 0, ½ and 1, a skin fade's
    foot, a stubble beard) is no shell and no coat but a SHADOW on the skin. The hair's colour is painted over it by
    the share its length covers (`clipCover`: about a third at clipper 0, about four fifths at clipper 1), mottled as
    follicles are, reaching the shell's own colour over its last 1.5 mm so the two meet with no ledge. The scalp's
    shell stops at the clipper's length, its edge smoothed, so a fade runs from the shell down through its shadow to
    the skin; a stubble shades the face and the throat alike, the neck's page as the head's. The length is the cut's
    own rule, smooth over the head (`dermal-hair.js` `growScalp` `clipOf`: the clipper's taper with no guide's own
    variation, the hairline averaged round the head), never the nearest guides' (their patches scalloped the fade's line
    and smeared its shadow); the recipe's `hairClip` carries it as a grid over the head for the skin's paint
    (`dermal-texture.js` `paintDermis` `clip`). The fade's cards fringe the hairline alone, never the fade's line. Never
    a solid helmet down to a fade's foot, never a stubble's blotchy coat.
  - THE SIDEBURN connects a fade to a beard, as a barber leaves it (`dermal-map.js` `sideburnOf`): where the face grows
    a beard, a band in front of the ear, from the beard's top on up until the scalp's own length is the longer, wears
    the beard's cheek length, both in the scalp's clipped length and in the paint (the dermis's own sideburn is a sliver
    over vellus skin, so a skin fade left bare skin between the hair and the beard). Its clipped length stays under the
    shell's, so a longer beard's sideburn is paint at full, never a strip of shell fringed with cards. The beard's paint
    over it adds only what the band left, so their overlap is never darker. A shaven face's fade takes the sideburn as
    it takes the rest.
  - THE BEARD FADE: with a beard, the side over the ear (from the sideburn back 60 mm behind the ear canal, above the
    ear's top) holds the same length, so the fade runs down to the beard's length there, never to a bald patch beside
    the sideburn; behind it the nape fades to the skin as the cut has it. Where the scalp's own paint is the fainter (the
    hairline's soft edge, a cell the clip has no length for), the band's shade is the one painted.
- **The ear raised** (realistic laws 10, `head-relational.js` `EAR_RAISE`): the ear sat low, its top 6 to 8 mm under the
  brow line and a man's lobule 4 mm under the nose's base. A laws 10 hero's ear is raised to the canon, its top at the
  brow line and its lobule at the nose's base (the face's own ear relations raised by the pole's amount). The ear's
  rim takes none of the hair's paint: the hero's skin chart knows the ear by its own parts, not by the box about it
  (`dermal-head.js` `headChartOf` `earAt`), and the hairline over the ear clears the ear's top by 12 mm
  (`dermal-map.js`; the head's marks carry the ear's top). A hero minted under earlier laws keeps its ear.
- A hero minted before keeps its blades byte for byte: the locks are its laws'.
