  turned under, the line from it climbing behind the jaw to under his ear and on into the back of the skull with no
  ledge to the nape, his ear set back over it, his chin forward; the female's brow and bridge the same, softer. New
  sculpt words for it: `earBack` (the ear set back along the head) and `napeLift` (the back of the head's underside
  raised behind the jaw, faded to nothing at the side seam).
- **Lifting the jaw's corner** to a figure's line was tried and set aside: raising the lower face's rows folds the face's
  front across the cheeks at any size that reads; the corner is set low and angled instead, the skull behind it lifted.
- **A high-schooler's body** (Shonen High's tune): skinnier from here on: the neck slim under the jaw, the arms and legs
  thinner, the waist and the chest's depth less, the shoulders a hair narrower, under the smaller head; the jaw's line
  reads against the neck. The body tune's new `neckGirth` (0.7 to 1.3) thins or thickens the neck, stored only when it
  moves off 1.
- **Shonen High's female after Nobara** (the north star): she wears the male's head (`head: 'male'` on her style
  entry: his skull, his profile, his jaw's line to the back of the skull, his ear), and over his face her own layer:
  her head smaller than his; her features softer (her brow's ridge, bridge and nose lighter, her jaw narrower, softer
  and turned under into a small pointed chin, her lids and brows less angled); her cheeks fuller; her eyes a little
  larger than his, almond under a heavier lash flicked at its tail; her brows thinner; her mouth smaller. Her body
  and her hair are her cast's. A style entry can lend a cast another base's head this way (`heroHeadPole`; the hair and
  the palette follow the cast, `heroHairPole`).
- **The jaw's line squared** (sculpt `jawLine`, a share, absent at 0; Shonen High's male at 1, and his female on his
  head): in profile the jaw's edge runs back from the chin nearly level to a corner set low under the ear, then
  straight up to it, and nothing hangs behind the chin. The side seam is drawn back toward the ramus by the column's
  nearness to it (the face's middle and the throat keep their place); the corner's lift comes off the sides, each point
  narrowed to the row it comes down to so the jaw keeps its V from the front; the underside behind the chin is raised
  onto the line from the chin's bottom to the corner by a smooth max. The male's lower cheeks fuller, rounding the
  face's side down to that edge.
- **The jaw's line, cleaned** (round two): the corner's lift taken off the sides narrows each point as the row twice as
  far below it, so from the front the jaw keeps the V the lift gave it and its lower rim no longer flares out; the
  line holds the face's side at the seam as well as the underside, the same from both, so the jaw's edge lies on it
  with no lip left below; the raise eased in behind the chin. Shonen High's chins a fifth narrower, his jaw's side
  curved in harder toward its edge (`jawHollow`), his female's with it.
- **A head seated back on the neck** (sculpt `seatBack`, of the head's height; the neck stays where it is): the head's
  registration moved back along its depth, the hair's body fit with it. Shonen High's female at 0.08: the male's head
  sat forward on her slimmer neck; seated back, her face stands as far before her neck as his before his. 
- **The keel under the chin merged** (round three): seen from below, the head's narrow bottom rows ran back from the
  chin as a keel with a jagged wall up each side to the wider floor. Behind the chin those rows now widen to the
  floor's width, so the keel and both walls curve into one piece, and the whole floor is then shrunk in toward the
  middle (the chin and the jaw's edge at the seam kept), so what shows from below is one smaller, rounded piece.
- **Shonen High's female, her lower face rounder**: her lower cheeks fuller and her jaw's side curved in less, so her
  face rounds out from the cheekbone down to the chin, the chin as pointed as before.
- **Shonen High's female toward Nobara's figure's proportions**: her eyes, as drawn (the lid band and lashes in
  them), about a quarter of her face's width and one eye's width apart, a little larger than his; her lower face
  shorter (her eye line lower in her head), her nose's tip and her lips lower, her nose smaller and lower in
  projection, her mouth narrower; her style's bands are the figure's measures, not the male's. A styled hero's sculpt
  words are read against their comfortable ranges only where the hero's own words move them off its form and style
  (`animeSculptBase`), as the hair's are: a style is its own canon.
- **Her cheeks taken back in**: the fuller lower cheeks of the round before read as chipmunk cheeks at three-quarter;
  her lower cheeks are now slimmer than his and her jaw's side curved in a little, so from the front and at
  three-quarter her face is one clean line from the cheekbone down to the pointed chin.
- **Her jaw from the front, one convex arc** (after the operator's drawn line): fuller along the jaw's edge from the
  nose's level down and narrowing into a narrower chin, so the outline is one curve from under the ear to the chin
  instead of a straight V meeting the cheek at a corner; at three-quarter it stays one smooth line.
- **Her nose and mouth raised**: her mouth moved up most of the way to where her nose's bottom was, and her nose's
  tip raised by the same amount under a root that stays, so the nose is shorter and steeper and the gap from it to
  the mouth is kept. All the way up, the mouth line sank into the nose's shadow and the nose all but flattened;
  three-quarters of the way reads.
- **Shonen High's bodies, proportioned** (on a proportion sheet: both casts at one scale, a line every head height):
  the male an athletic lead's, 7.65 heads (the torso shorter and the legs longer, the shoulders broader over a narrow
  waist, a V); the female long-legged and slim, 7.26 heads (the torso shorter, the legs longer, the waist narrow, the
  shoulders narrower).
- **The body rounded** (`body-smooth.js`; a style's `smooth`, Shonen High's 1; the recipe's `smoothBody: { rounds }`):
  the body's skin split once, each triangle into four, its new points on the curved patch its corners' welded normals
  describe (the curved PN triangle's edge), so the silhouette reads rounded rather than as its rings' facets. The
  corners keep their places byte for byte (the joints, the pinned parts' seats, the binds); a new point is appended
  after every point the mesh had and binds as its two corners' mean; a part's open rim splits on its straight line.
  Absent, the mesh as built. One round: the parts are still separate shells, so the seams where they meet (the chest's
  plates on the torso, the torso over the pelvis) still read; fusing them is the next step.
- **A style's chest** (`chest`: its pectorals' and its bust's own words over the form's, hero-form.js heroPlan `chest`):
  a pectoral's `rise` lifts the dome off its lower border over that share of the run instead of standing its full
  height there, so the muscle grows out of the chest rather than lying on it as a panel; a bust's `size`, its field's
  words and `within` (held inside a share of the torso's half-width), each absent as it was. Shonen High's male: thinner pectorals rising
  over 0.45 of the run (once the body was rounded they read as separate panels).
- **A chest's width** (`chest.width`: the rib cage's ring, the shoulders' span left as the tune sets it; the tune has no
  key for it, `shoulders` moves the arms' span alone). Shonen High's both at 0.82, their chests' depth a little less: the
  rounded body stood too broad under the arms, its sides flaring out past the armpit; they now fall nearly straight to
  the waist.
- **Shonen High's chests, simpler**: the male's pectoral layer gone (a chest's `pec: false`: the chest the torso's own
  smooth front; rounded, the layer read as an imprint), the female's bust a fifth smaller than the form's
  (`bust: { size: 0.8 }`).

### Broadcasting personas: the realistic head reads a script, for games

- **A persona reads a script in a delivery register** (`control/lib/graph/persona/`). A register is a card, as an emote
  is: its pace and articulation, the gaps it breathes in, the words it stresses (names, numbers, by how many a
  sentence), where it looks (the lens, its notes), its resting face and the body's gestures for its stresses, its
  asides and its close. `readScript` compiles plain text (`*stress*`, `[pause]`, `[pause 1.5]`, `(aside)`, a blank line
  a new paragraph) into the face's beats (perform.js), the lines and their words timed on one clock, captions (SRT,
  VTT) and a body track; the same script in the same register is the same read. First registers: `anchor`, `briefing`,
  `speech`, `documentary`, `play-by-play`.
- **The face is gen-7's** (`speakerFidelity`): a talking face only where a game reads in the `gen-7` era and the speaker
  is a realistic hero; anywhere else the same read gives its audio, its captions and the body's gestures.
- **A persona is a record of its own**: `create_character({ as: 'persona', spec: { hero, voice?, register?, reads } })`
  mints kind `persona`, pointing at a hero (its body and face) and a voice register, keeping the scripts it reads by id;
  every read regenerates from its script. The door answers each read in short (its seconds, lines, words, the words it
  stressed, its captions and gestures) and where its face is drawn. `update_character` merges its reads by id (null
  removes one), checks the record whole and its refs before storing, and keeps what it replaced as a revision. A
  persona is turned and exported as its hero (the object shelf): its World and its GLB play the hero, its reads the
  realistic face's `face:<id>` clips; `export_model` writes each read's captions (`captions/<id>.srt`, `.vtt`) and
  cue sheet (`cues/<id>.json`: lines, words, stresses, gaze, gestures, the clip it rides) beside the model. Manual:
  `get_solid_vocab({ id: 'persona' })`; routing card `persona`.
- **The first host: a news broadcast on a screen in a world.** A world's `broadcasts` key (`[{ persona, read, at, yaw?,
  size?, title?, strap?, package?, loop?, gap? }]`, `persona/screen.js`) stands screens in it, each playing one read on
  a loop on the read's own clock: the set in a broadcast package's glass, the channel's bug, the reader as the body
  plays the read (a nod, a point, a bow on its gestures, its mouth on its words), the lower third and the captions
  (`scene/channels/broadcast-screen.js`, an appended page row: zero bytes when absent). The page draws no talking face
  yet; each screen records the fidelity its world's era gives it. Godot and Roblox mark it absent (the persona's export
  carries the face clips, captions and cue sheets).

### Cavern water: lakes, rivers and falls underground

- **A river underground** (`trail.ground.cavern` with `water.river`): it runs between the cavern's end walls, rising
  out of the rock at one end and sinking into it at the other, a dark mouth in the wall at each; before, its water
  climbed the end walls to the cavern's rim.
- **No sea under the rock**: a coast on a cavern's trail (the cube's or the trail's own) is skipped and named in the
  water's forms (`skipped`), as a lake with no room is; before, the sea's level was read off the raised wall and its
  sheet hung inside the cave.
- **Underground water reads as underground**: in a cavern, the water (a lake, a river, a pool, a crossing's stream) is
  deepened toward the dark and shows less of its bed, so only the cavern's lamps, cracks and skylight light it; a
  fall's white water stays white. A trail without a cavern draws its water as before, to the byte.

### Compose geocity: a metro's map, its major streets first, on land that falls to its water

A metro (`lib/graph/geocity/`) laid at its widest grain before anything inside it: its major streets first, carving
its neighbourhoods, each in a ring out from its core, on land that rises and falls. The base is the fractal city's
metro as `city/plan/` reads it into metres (its grammars: sections, towers, skins); the discipline is the geotown's
(every square metre once, laws that advise, a sheet before a scene). Built toward its games: city hunter, and the
Quest Open World (the walled-core dungeon's opposite pole: a map that opens sideways, connected and loaded as it is
passed, a city or an island). Built as the geocube kind's `show: 'geocity'`, the whole metro as massing.

- **A metro is a card** (`geocity/metro.js` METROS): its extent, its water (a shore along a side; all four an island),
  its core's seat, its land's FALL (metres toward a side: downtown down its spine to the lake) and the hills over it
  (a painted landscape's), its arterials' spacing (tight at the seat, looser past `reach`), its rings' reaches, its
  heights, its green budget, its streets inside a neighbourhood (`streets`: the collector's span, the civic block's
  least) and its segments' weights by ring, its city grammar (`city/plan` grammars) and its outskirts' geotown pattern. Two starters:
  `lakeshore` (a Toronto: the core by the lake, the land falling to the shore, the grid loosening northward) and
  `harbour-island` (the core on a harbour at the west shore, hills inland, water all round). A recipe's settings lay
  over its metro's (an object merged all the way down); anything off the card is refused by name.
- **The map** (`geocity/design.js` designGeocity), layer by layer, each its own dice:
  - the LAND inside its water: the natural ground (the fall plus the hills) and the streets' ground, smoothed so an
    arterial keeps the land's grade and not its every hummock;
  - the ARTERIALS: the SPINE through the seat each way, then arterials stepped out to the land's edge, each step rolled
    inside the rail at its distance; each in its grammar's major section, its profile along the ground (its ends'
    heights, its steepest grade);
  - the NEIGHBOURHOODS they enclose, each its RING by its middle's distance from the seat (the four round the seat
    always the core; the frame the lower tall; the outskirts four storeys and lower), its sides (an arterial, the water,
    or the BEYOND past the map's land edge, where a geotown joins later) and its PORTS (each arterial side, its run and
    its ends' heights);
  - the GREEN from the top: the city park reserved whole (a frame neighbourhood clear of the map's edge, by dice), the
    rest of the share given out as quotas by area times the ring's weight;
  - the REGION GRAPH: each neighbourhood a node, each pair across an arterial an edge with its PORTAL and its height,
    and the neighbourhoods open to the beyond: what a Quest Open World streams as it is passed;
  - the HEIGHTS (`geocity/heights.js`, the card's `heights`), in storeys, the highest read winning at a point: each
    ring's MEDIAN from its outer reach to its inner, geometrically, inside its RAIL (the core's towers, the frame's lower
    tall, the outskirts at four storeys and lower), so the skyline falls outward; secondary NODES, every `every`-th spine
    crossing out past the core (a Yonge and Bloor), the four neighbourhoods round one BUILT as the ring inside theirs and
    the median rising toward it; and each arterial's FRONTAGE, a band `depth` metres deep along a neighbourhood's
    arterial side, rising to its corridor's storeys (a spine's more than an arterial's) where its ring's rail stops short:
    mid-rise lining a main street past the core. Each neighbourhood carries the ring it `builds` as, its interior's
    storeys (median and rail) and each frontage's; `storeysAt(x, y)` reads the field anywhere;
  - each neighbourhood's own PARK (`geocity/parks.js`, the card's `green.park`) out of its quota by its ring's share,
    laid before its streets so they go round it: a band along the shore on the water (a lakeshore park), else a rect
    inside its interior clear of its frontages, its aspect rolled; under the least none, the quota left to its segments;
  - the BLOCKS inside each neighbourhood (`geocity/blocks.js`), each its own dice: COLLECTORS across a neighbourhood
    wider than the card's span (a geotown main street's section), moved off its park to run along it; a street round
    the park (a strip under a block's least between it and an edge the park's, so it may take a strip of frontage);
    LOCALS between those, each gap cut into whole blocks of its ring's length (the grammar's square pitch in the core
    and the frame, in its minor section; the geotown's long blocks running north and south in the outskirts, in its
    street's section), cut where they would cross the park. Each block a BLOCK SEGMENT by ring (`geocity/segments.js`):
    the core's `tower` (a podium, a tower or two on its corners rising past the block's median, the core's tail; a
    plaza, a laneway, a ramp) and `podium` by weight, its `square` at its middle; the frame's `midrise` (round a planted
    court) on an arterial and `slab` (on its lawn, the lower tall) by weight; the outskirts the geotown's own segments:
    an `edge` where an arterial runs along a block's long side, a `main-street` where a collector does (a short end on
    either is its houses' corners), a `school` at its middle, `houses`, `apartments` and `lowrise` by weight. The civic
    block (the square, the school) the one nearest the middle, off the arterials where one is. Each block's storeys off
    the field inside its ring's rail (on an arterial its frontage's), and its GROUND its segment's shares of its area:
    the geocity's own surfaces (podium, building, plaza, planting, court, lawn, laneway, ramp, lot) in the core and the
    frame, and in the outskirts the geotown's, read from the geotown's own design of each segment with its streets left
    out, so an outskirts block keeps a geotown's measures;
  - the LEDGER: water, the arterials (each crossing once), parks and neighbourhoods, by ring; inside each neighbourhood
    its streets, blocks and park, and every block's ground by surface, summed for the metro; the green budget,
    reserved, given out as quotas, placed as the neighbourhoods' parks and grown as soft ground.
- **The laws** (`geocity/laws.js`), advice only: `closes`, `grade`, `rings`, `green`, `holds` (every outskirts
  neighbourhood holds a geotown neighbourhood of its pattern, two blocks by two), `ports`, and the Quest Open World's
  `open` (one part) and `sideways` (no bridge in the region graph: always two ways round); the heights' `skyline` (each
  ring's builders lower on the whole than the ring inside), `caps` (every interior and frontage inside its rail) and
  `interior` (a neighbourhood keeps ground behind its frontages); `parks` (placed as the quotas ask, inside); the
  blocks' `blocks` (each neighbourhood's ground once, each block's surfaces its area), `pitch` (blocks inside their
  ring's length), `segments` (each its ring's, the civic blocks), `soft` (each neighbourhood's green ground most of its
  quota) and `towers` (past their podiums, inside their rail, the tallest in the core).
- **Built** (`geocity/scene.js`, the geocube kind's `show: 'geocity'`, `geocity: { … }` its recipe): the metro stood
  on the cube's land at its hour, in metres, as MASSING, under a face budget (`faces`, advice): the water a plane along
  each shore carried out to the horizon (a shore looks over open water, an island stands in it); the arterials a road
  between two walks over a kerb, each neighbourhood's ground its streets, a walk round every block, all draped on the
  streets' ground in cells; each block a pad in TERRACES along its long side, each level over its walk at its highest
  corner, retaining faces down to the walk and the terrace below; the buildings by segment on their terraces (a tower
  block's podium and towers, a podium block, a square's planting and kiosk, a mid-rise ring round its court, a slab on
  its lawn and its lot; in the outskirts semi pairs under gables to the street in two rows back to back, an edge's two
  storeys and a main street's three of shops along their street, low-rises, a walk-up, a school and its field), glass
  in the core, stone and brick outward from its grammar's skins; past dusk each tall wall's floors lit in runs (the
  grammar's share and palette), panes no light shades, none by day. Lit and hazed by the cube at its hour (the city's
  haze per metre); seen from its water (the skyline), over it, its core and up its spine, walked from the seat, the
  dummy round the block nearest it. The answer's `geocity`: the counts, the ledger, the neighbourhoods, the region
  graph, the laws. `scripts/spikes/geocity/geocity.mjs --hours noon,night` captures it. Lakeshore: 8,019 buildings,
  131 towers, 87.7k faces by day, 12.5k lit panes at night.
- **Evoked at game scale** (`geocity.evoke`, metro.js EVOKES; design.js `evoked`): a game does not take the metro to
  scale, it evokes a piece of it. `skyline` the whole metro's tall buildings and water; `neighbourhood` one (`at`, by
  default the core's nearest the seat); `corridor` an arterial's frontage end to end (`along`, by default the spine
  from the shore inland: a Yonge); `segment` one block (`at`, by default a tower block by the seat); `metro` every block
  to scale. An evocation is at GAME scale unless it says (`play: 'game' | 'real'`, metro.js PLAY): what a walker covers
  compressed as city/plan's game scale does (the map, the arterials' spacing, the rings, a node's reach, the
  collector's span ×0.6; a frontage's and a block's rows' depth ×0.8; the grammar at its game play; the outskirts'
  geotown blocks), never a storey, a lane or a door. Built in three tiers: the evoked blocks at a building's DETAIL,
  each core and frame mass a lot the facade pipeline wears (city/plan/facades.js: curtainwall, punched stone, brick,
  a tower's shape; its windows lit at night on the facades' own grids) brought from its units back to metres; the
  neighbourhoods round them as massing; the rest its skyline (one coarse drape a neighbourhood, its tall buildings, its
  low fabric a flat mass along each long side). Seen first from over what it evokes and from its own street, where
  its walk starts. Its `evokes` law (advice) holds it to the metro to scale designed beside it on the same seed: each
  ring's mix of segments and its storeys, its green share, its towers a core block. An outskirts block keeps its
  massing at detail until it is a geotown's.
- **Roads** (`geocity/roads.js`, the card's `roads`): each arterial its own cross-section, laid band by band from its
  centre out between the grammar's walks, its right-of-way its own (the neighbourhoods beside it stand off its half;
  the ledger sums each). A major street FOUR LANES, two each way, parking at each kerb; a share carry a SPACER between
  their directions (`median`: a planted median over a kerb), most do not; one-way PAIRS by the core (the two nearest
  parallel arterials off the spine, east-west first: a Richmond and an Adelaide), THREE LANES the same way each, the
  pair's two opposite, a bike lane on one side; STREETCAR rails (Toronto's broad gauge) on the spines and on a share
  of the rest, in the inner lanes, or down the spacer in their own right-of-way where the street has one (a Spadina).
  Lanes never compress at game scale. Each band carries its way (`dir`, the grammar's traffic side: left where it
  drives on the left), so the lines are a lane graph a driver reads later.
- **The street, near** (`geocity/kit.js`): the metro city's own doodads at true size, its kerb lamps and signals,
  street-name signs and tram poles (fractal-city.js `kerbLamp`, `intersectionDoodads`) made round by its round kit
  (city/round-kit.js: a tapered standard on its collar, a lathed head, lenses, galvanized posts), each baked once a
  facing; and the paint and rails as flat pieces. Along every arterial: its lane lines dashed between lanes one way, a
  double yellow between a two-way street's directions where no spacer parts them, solid white at its parking and bike
  lanes, a bike lane painted green; its rails end to end and the overhead (a pole at each kerb, a span across, a
  contact wire over each track); lamps at both kerbs at the metro's stride, staggered. At each crossing crosswalks on
  every arm, a signal on each corner (every crossing signalled, the metro's way) its mast over the lanes, a street-name
  sign, and on a streetcar line a stop each way past it (a platform and its shelter down a right-of-way). All stamped
  as instanced repeats drawn only NEAR the camera: from far the blocks suffice. A `crossing` camera on an evocation.
- **The ground, near** (visual interest where the eye is): the ground and the masses in their material words laid as
  tiles (era/arch-style.js `wordTile`, era/town-dress.js `dressTownFace`, texel × the baked light): the roads asphalt,
  the walks scored pavement, a hard block's pad (a tower's, a podium's, a square's, a mid-rise's) flags, a streetcar
  right-of-way setts, retaining faces sawn stone; houses, shops, mid-rise, low-rises and schools brick, podiums sawn
  stone, slabs precast. A glass tower's walls take the sun's sheen (`spec`, the specular channel). The furniture, near:
  on the arterials a bin by each crossing, hydrants, and where close-built benches with bike rings, newspaper boxes at
  a corner, a bench at each streetcar stop, street trees in their pits clear of the lamps; on a neighbourhood's own
  streets wooden hydro poles with their crossarms, wires and hung lamps and verge trees in the outskirts, the metro's
  kerb lamps and bins in the core and frame; round a square benches, bins and bollards (kit.js: the metro's park bin,
  bollard, power pole and bench at a person's size, round by its kit). The trees grown from the vegetation library
  (`plantPool` / `plantRepeats`, crowns raised over the walk), drawn near the camera like the kit. Lit live: under
  live shadows (`ctx.liveSun`) every face carries its sun share (city/plan's key share), a lit window its own light.
  Not yet: relief on the paved ground (gen-7's ground parallax reads natural soil and scree only, so a paved kind is a
  new shader's), and a sky's reflection on outdoor glass (only water, a wet road and a room's panes take one).
- **The city changing** (`segments.js` LIVELY, the card's `lively`: each ring's shares, on each block's own dice, off
  its civic block): a share of the blocks a BUILDING GOING UP (`construction`: what it `becomes` and its `progress`, its
  columns and floor slabs risen that far, its concrete core above them, a tower crane over it, seen from afar; near the
  camera scaffolding up its long faces, a bay every 2 m and every lift, plywood hoarding along its streets and
  temporary fence panels round the rest, barriers and cones on its walk), a surface PARKING lot (asphalt, its stalls in
  rows across an aisle, their lines and cars in most, each its paint as an instance's tint), a VACANT lot (scrub over
  old gravel behind temporary fencing). New kit (kit.js): scaffold bay, fence panel, hoarding, barrier, cone, car,
  stall line; new surfaces `site` (gravel) and `scrub` (soft).
- **The geotown composed in** (`geocity/towns.js`, the recipe's `geotowns`): the two tools composable at any grain and
  anywhere (the edge or the core), on the metro's land (the geotown's design and scene take the metro's natural ground
  in their frame: `field`, geotown/scene.js's `ctx.field`, absent as before). A NEIGHBOURHOOD (`'D3': true`) laid by the
  geotown fitted inside it: the outskirts' pattern to scale (compressed as the metro's own at game scale), as many
  blocks as it holds (a block segment of its ring's where none fits), its streetscape by its ring (leafy in the
  outskirts, snug in the frame, urban in the core), centred, the green round its frame; or the town its recipe asks
  (`{ neighbourhood: 'annex' }`, a layout, an evocation: named, its evocation implied). A BLOCK (`'D3.2.1'`) laid by
  one of the geotown's block segments (the block's own if it is one, else its ring's: houses, a low-rise, a main
  street; or `{ segment }`): its rows as deep as the metro's block shares across them (a lane's or an alley's share
  given back) and as many houses, shops or low-rises along them as the block runs, cropped to its block and centred in
  the metro's, its ground the town block's ledger and the green round it. Built by the geotown's own scene in its place
  (its trees near the camera only); as the skyline, its houses as boxes. A geotown's laws are its own advice, read
  beside it; the metro's `geotowns` law holds each inside its place. A quest open world's regions take them as they
  are (a geotown's neighbourhood is a region).
- **The quest open world** (`lib/graph/qow/qow.js`, a `design_game` world's `qow`; `docs/quest-open-world.md`; the
  `gameworld-qow` card): the walled-core dungeon's opposite pole. Its regions a geocity's neighbourhoods and its region
  graph (`map: { geocity, seed? }`), its `spawn` (the core's by the seat), optional `locks` (the WCD's gates: a
  clearance or a power, never the way on), `quests` (main or side, `after` others), `landmarks` ('auto': the core's
  tallest tower and each node's, seen thirty times their height off), its `stream` rings (a region and its neighbours
  `hops` away, what is loaded as it is passed), the `level` it is played in. Its principles as laws, advice in
  design_game's readout (`advice.qow`): `open`, `sideways` (no cut vertex among the open regions), `unforced`, `seen`,
  `streamed`, `spread`. Malformed is refused by name.
- **Near repeats** (`scene/scene-three.js`): a repeat may say `near` (world units): the page cuts its instances into
  square tiles, each its own instanced mesh on the shared geometry, shown only while the camera stands within `near`
  of it, checked before each render (so a capture, a frozen frame and the live loop agree); a textured template's faces
  (a tree's bark) tiled the same on their own material. A world without one gains not a byte.
- **The sheet** (`geocity/sheet.js`), three views of one map: `rings` (each neighbourhood by the ring it builds as,
  shaded by its ground's height), `heights` (each by its median storeys, each arterial frontage band by its own) and
  `blocks` (its streets, the collectors darker, its blocks by segment, the towers on them); `focus` crops it round a
  few neighbourhoods; the spine darker, the parks, the nodes, the portals, the crossings' heights, the ledger and the
  laws. `scripts/spikes/geocity/geocity.mjs` writes each, and the blocks cropped round the core.

### Foe casting call: the cast sheet

A world's foes had no page. The bestiary, the resolver and the Mind facet already said everything about each foe: its
class, rank, numbers, mind, modes, states, death and relations. No book showed it. This theme adds the cast sheet, a
fourth book beside the world, character and feel books, and a casting call that proposes a cast for a world that fights
and keeps none.

- **The cast sheet** (`/api/sketches/<ref>/bible?book=foes`, `gameworld/foe-cast-html.js`). It reads the world's foes
  through `gameworld/foe-cast.js` `foeCastOf`, which only reads what the shelves already say.
  - The lineup plate: every foe at the stature it reads at in the game, beside the hero, on a metre rule.
  - A tile per foe by tier. Its portrait is the figure a run made (the sketch's PNG while served, none in a download),
    else its silhouette.
  - A card per foe: the lesson it teaches the player, its numbers, its attack's timing, its mind as the Mind facet
    resolves it on its body, its shelves, and what each engine keeps.
  - The game's flavor sets the stat words (`STAT_WORDS`: a platformer counts bops and hearts, a realistic game shows
    health). The register sets the sheet's title and tier names (`REGISTER_WORDS`: anime or western).
  - It is a gate like the other books: `foes:cast` and `foes:<id>` are parts with prints, approved or sent back
    through `design_game`. They never hold a run back.
- **The casting call** (`gameworld/foe-casting.js` `castingCall`). It proposes a cast of four roles (grunt, harrier,
  elite, boss) from the intent cube's Mind values and combat, the flavor, the era's people and the target engine, with
  every choice's reasons.
  - A class the cube's `mind.foes` names is cast first.
  - One people, rolled from the era for the whole cast, wears every class that stands on two legs. A platformer keeps
    the stand-in beasts.
  - It is proposed and never written. `design_game`'s readout carries it as a `foes` step with the patch that writes
    it, and the sheet shows it until a bestiary is written.
- **A person dressed as a crew** (`foes/dress.js`). `skin: { people: 'human', dress: { faction, kind?, colourway?,
  body? } }` dresses a soldier, a guard or a cultist from the comic hero pack's grunt factions: the kind's build,
  clothes, headgear and gear, and the crew's colours.
  - Made through the hero door (`foes-<id>`, its reactions on it) and stood on the library as any made person. The
    pack's baked golden light is left off, so a foe stands in its world's light. `body: 'realistic'` draws it on the
    realistic body.
  - Only a person is dressed, and the dress names its build and age; its facets name only its pole.
  - The casting call dresses a cast of people as one crew (`ERA_DRESS`): its faction by era, a soldier's for a shooter
    or a stealth game, its colourway rolled, each role a kind of it and the boss the heaviest. A modern stealth world
    is cast as private military in one colourway.
- **Foes in a building's rooms.** `levels.<id>.foes` now stands on a building level, each room between the way in and
  the goal a beat. Without a count a building stands `ROOM_FOES` of its rooms, spread from the way in to the goal (an
  office has dozens of rooms). The walker or the hero in it takes their hits as on a trail: a building level now lays
  its extra's `pilot` as a trail level does, and no building cast carried one before, so no building level moves. A
  building made by ref still takes none. The casting call places foes in buildings too, its boss one of it.
- **The patrol** (`foes/classes/patrol.js`, the `patrol` move in `foes/vocab.js` and `worlds/controllable/foe.js`). It
  walks its round between two posts and back, watching ahead. A hero in its sight (the mind's range and cone, and a
  clear line past the colliders) hands it to the mind that same step, which perceives the hero and engages. Once the
  mind has seen no one for `calm` seconds, it walks its round again. Web only: Godot and Roblox are marked absent. The
  regenerated hill-climb page moves by its lift (Godot 46 → 48 of 500 rolled worlds).
- **Oozes as variants.** A beast grown by oozes is a variant of the same class on the same species grown by none.
  - The cast sheet reads each ooze at its strength and its stylism, draws a variant in its ooze's own colour (the ooze
    row's tint) outlined in its tier's, names the two to each other, and says that an ooze grows a beast's shape, never
    its stature.
  - The casting call grows a beast cast by the world's oozes: its character book's elements (`ELEMENT_OOZE`) and its
    era's (`ERA_OOZES`), at most `MAX_VARIANTS`. It makes a variant of each beast role per ooze, met from the second
    level on, and grows the boss itself (`BOSS_OOZE`, dire, with the world's first). A growth that no longer fits its
    class is left off and said.
- **The sheet in its world's colours.** The cast sheet is drawn as the world's bible is:
  - The lineup stands on the world's own sky and ground (its kit's colour key), and the page's accent is the kit's
    paint.
  - The cover takes the lineup as its plate, with the strip of levels in the order they are played, each showing who
    stands on it.
  - The casting call is the bible's own blocks: the ledger of what it read, a civilization's article for each role (its
    plate beside the hero, why this class, its variants, its dress), and the strip of who would stand where.
  - The play order moved from the world bible into `gameworld/graph.js` (`playOrder`), shared by both.
- **Cards said to a player.** Each card leads with what the foe does, how to beat it and what it costs.
  - "How to beat it" is rows (`COUNSEL`): a line for each word the foe carries that a player can answer (its attack,
    its tell's seconds, its stomp, its sight, its memory, cover, a pack, a duelist's switches, its modes, its summons
    or pair, a state).
  - "What it costs" is a sentence in the flavor's words ("2 bops to down; a touch costs you 1 heart").
  - The mind's situations, the engine marks and the gate fold into "For the designer".
- **Real figures.** A foe a run has made is photographed as the table game's book photographs its cast
  (`lib/mcp/tools/foe-portraits.js` over `photographCharacter`, now exported from `table-rpg-portraits.js`). Its tile
  shows the figure and its card the bust, in the cast sheet and the world bible, a download included. A foe not made,
  or with no browser, keeps its silhouette, which also stands in for a photograph that fails to load. The lineup and
  the level strips stay a scale drawing. Seen in this container: a frost wolf made through the animal door, photographed
  in about 6 s, shown on its tile and card through the route.
- **The cast in the world's bible and on the dashboard.**
  - The world bible has a Foes section (the lineup and the tiles, each linked to its card on the cast sheet) and, on
    each level, who stands on it. A world that fields none carries not a byte of it.
  - The world's rail has a Foes outcome (the cast sheet's parts, read on the cast sheet) and a Foes exit. A world
    without foes keeps its outcomes as they were.
- **Kinds by what they carry.** A dressed role takes the kind its class reads as: a class on watch a kind whose arms are
  stowed (the sentry), one that fires a long gun at the ready (the rifleman), the boss or a heavy class the heaviest
  build (the breacher). The stealth outpost's guard on post is now its sentry.
- The `gameworld-foes` card names the dress and a building's rooms and gains the patrol's row. Its ceiling is re-pinned
  at 5120 bytes (4916), with the reason beside the pin.
- `node scripts/out-sheet.mjs foes [--genre <id>] [--propose]` writes the sheet for the example world.
- `docs/foes.md` has the sheet and the casting call. The `gameworld-foes` and `gameworld-next` cards name them.

Machine gate: `gameworld/foe-cast.test.js`, `foes/dress.test.js`, the building and dressed cases in
`gameworld/foes.test.js` and the patrol in `worlds/controllable/foe.test.js` pass. They cover one case per procedure (a
beast, a people, a model, a mode chain, a summoner, a counting flavor and a health flavor, the gate going stale, a
dressed person, a building's rooms, a patrol seen and unseen, a variant and its oozes), plus the casting call adopted
as written, the intent's classes first, a people's era, a platformer's beasts, a dressed crew, ooze variants met deeper
in, the sheet in its world's colours, a card's counsel and cost, photographs with their fallback, the world bible's Foes
section (and none without foes), kinds by what they carry, the rail's Foes outcome, and absence. Eyes gate: not run. The operator
looks at a platformer world's sheet and a shooter world's, and at a dressed soldier made through the door.

### Geocube water: the ground it keeps

- **The substrate reads the water** (`era/substrate.js`, the water from `era/out-water.js`): a lake's, a pool's or a
  river's shallows (up to 0.6 m under its level) are wet ground, deeper water and the sea are no land at all, the shore
  the water lays as sand (a lake's ring, a beach, a river's shingle) is sand, and a fresh water's bank low over it
  (0.9 m, within its reach) is wet. Before, only a crossing's stream wet the ground, and a lake, a coast or a river read
  as soil, so a biocube's swarms and a sandstone strand never found their shores. A stage with no water reads as
  before, cell for cell. The water reports `level(x, y)`: the fresh water whose bank holds a point.
- **The flora page counts the water** (`docs/flora-gaps.md`, `levelShares` in `era/substrate-flora.js`): each cube
  preset is read dry and by each water a word lays (lake, coast, river), and a level is half of each. Sand and wet
  ground, 0% of a level before, are now 3.4% each (6.7% and 6.9% of a waterside level), so the wet-ground and
  sand-ground wants rank on the ground they would cover instead of the 2% floor.

### Headgear as a library, and the comic hero pack's characters by name

Operator: "i need the comic pack to load character and assets more than anything else in comics"; "lift headgear into a
general library and build it". Nothing outside the comic hero pack (and the foes, through its grunts) read its headgear,
its cast or its crews; no tool reached them.

- **The headgear library** (`lib/graph/headgear/cards.js`): the comic hero pack's headgear cards moved out of the pack,
  beside the helmets by tradition (`helmets.js`). Masks, cowls, eyegear, mouthpieces, helmets, respirators and visors,
  each a card in the hero door's own words per body. Its errors say `headgear:`; its shell table is `HELMET_SHELLS`
  (the tradition library owns `HELMETS`). The pack, its grunts and the foes read it from there. Nothing they make
  changes: a move, not an edit.
- **`headgear` on the hero door** (`headgear/wear.js`, `layered.js`): a card's id, or a helmet by tradition. The hero
  stores the word alone and lowers it on every read, after a sport's `kit` (`wornHero`), so
  `update_character { spec: { headgear } }` swaps it in place and `null` takes it off.
  - A hero wearing a word is the hero with the card applied by hand, plan for plan.
  - The card's colours sit beneath the hero's `palette`, so naming a group (Helmet, Mask, EyeLens …) recolours it.
  - The game body wears every word. The realistic body wears the domino and the cowl and refuses the others by name.
  - A helmet by tradition becomes the outfit build's `language.head`, keeping a cover, band, net or mount the language
    already names; with no outfit build it is refused.
  - An unknown word is refused with the nearest word. A word the door does not take (`helmet`, `mask`, `cowl`,
    `goggles`, `visor`, `hat`) points at `headgear`.
  - Absent, no key and every byte as it was.
- **The comic hero pack's characters by name** (`cosmos/packs/index.js`): `create_character { pack: { id: 'comic-hero',
  member | grunt, look?, … } }`.
  - `member`: a cast member, with `era`, `pole`, `seed`, `headgear`, `pieces`, `accessories`, `items` (or
    `'signature'`), `ensemble` and `swing`.
  - `grunt`: a crew's grunt, with `kind`, `colourway`, `pole`, `seed` and `index`.
  - `look`: a stop of the dial, `dcau-golden` (the western hero on the game body) when none is named.
  - The pack's own orders are minted through the hero door with the headgear left as the door's word
    (`memberOrders` and `gruntOrders` take `words: true`), so the character is the same hero and stays editable by word.
    A grunt's crew colours stay over its head's.
  - A hero's `spec` beside `pack` lays over the pack's. The result says what was rolled (`pack`). One schema property
    on `create_character`.
- **Found and read**: generated solid-vocab cards, built from the tables at load: `headgear` (every word by family, the
  bodies it fits) and `comic-hero` (the cast, the looks, the eras, the cards, the crews, how to call them). The layered
  card's `hero-headgear` section. A `comic-hero` routing card ("a superhero and his henchmen", "put a cowl with bat ears
  on my hero"), `headgear` on the `revise-character` card, and two routing-eval rows.
- Machine gate: `headgear/wear.test.js`, `headgear/entries.test.js`, `hero-headgear.test.js` (one card per family
  through the door, the swap and the removal through `update_character`), `create-character.pack.test.js` (a member
  with each family's card as the word equals the member with it worn; a grunt with a head; the refusals; a mint through
  the door), the pack's own tests and the tests the change reaches. Eyes gate not run: nobody has looked at a pack
  member made through the door, or at a swap.
- Stopping point: the realistic head is fitted for two words; the pack's pieces, accessories and ensembles ride a
  member's orders, not the hero door; the pack's cubes are not yet read by `design_game`.

### One body for every tiered hero

- **The form body** (`hero-form.js` `FORM_BODY`, `formBodied`, hero laws 21): one body for every tiered hero, whatever
  head it wears; only the head makes a difference, the body by its cast's sizes and proportions alone. It is the anime
  adult's body since laws 20 (rounded, the rib cage narrower under the shoulders, no male pectoral layer), named for
  what it is (`anime-looks.js` `ANIME_FORM_BODY` is it), and the landmark head's adult wears it now too: the same
  rounding, the same chest, and on the lit export the engine's smooth normals over the whole figure, the western face
  smooth with it. A row stamped before laws 21 keeps
  its body. Not yet on a hero robot's toy body, an undead's or a beast-kin's, nor on a child or a chibi (its build's).
- **The rounded female's hip read as the plateau it is** (`FORM_BODY.coreBands`): rounded, the female's hip side falls
  from its waist ring nearly straight to the trochanter, so its widest stretch is a plateau under 2 mm flat from the hip
  joint down; the core advice reads its peak anywhere on it instead of warning that it stands above the trochanter.
- **The stretch audit reads a rounded body** (`hero-stretch.js` `shellRings`): a rounded body's new points carry their
  edge's first corner's station and slot (`mix`, `body-smooth.js`), and the audit's ring map took them in the corners'
  places, so on a rounded body (the anime adult's since laws 20) its rings were midpoints and its seams read nothing.
  The new points are on no ring now.

### Water live: a geocube's river, falls and lake drawn as they move in gen-7

- **The water's plan** (`era/out-water.js` `plan`): a trail's river (its line downstream, its levels, its width, how far
  it falls), its falls (the lip, the drop, the width, the brook to it, the pool's carved bed) and its lake (its carved
  bed, a few leaves on it) as data, each body's
  painted faces carrying its id (`waterBody`).
- **Drawn live in gen-7** (`era/water-live.js`, read in `worlds/world-scene.js`): a gen-7 read on the World page draws
  the river on the surface channel's river (ripples and streaks running downstream, lanes along the banks, a narrow
  band of foam at them, the river look tinted by the cube's water, its current as fast as its bed falls), and the falls
  as a sheet jet off the lip (glassy over the brink, whitening as it falls, mist at its foot) into its pool, a shallows
  pond in the pool's own carved bed that the fall churns; the brook to the lip a small river. The painted sheets they
  replace are left out, so the form render never draws them as its still mirror. gen-6, an export (`paint`) and a
  cavern keep the painted water, every byte as before.
- **The lake as still water** (gen-7): a shallows pond in its own carved bed, still but for a breeze's faint ripples
  and the rings where it is waded or rained on, a few leaves at rest on it, in the lake look tinted by the cube's water
  and as dark with depth as the river beside it (`absorb`, below). gen-6 and the exports keep its painted sheet.
- **A water look's own absorption** (`materials/aqua-look.js` `absorb`: r/g/b per metre over the preset's `sigma`): a
  world's water as dark with depth as its own. Absent, every look as before.
- **A pool in its own bed** (`materials/shallows.js`): a pond takes a world's carved basin (`bed`: a grid of depths
  under its level) instead of its lobed bowl.
- **A falls' pool on a river**: where a far-side river runs past the falls' foot, the pool is laid at the river's level
  there, so the fall drops into the river. Before, the river's channel cut the pool's rim and its water stood over the
  channel beside it, its edge in the air (both eras).
- `scripts/spikes/water/live.mjs`: a geocube's water from each still in gen-6 and gen-7, each at two moments apart.

### The muscle shirt: a flat body puts it on and its muscles show up (the Saikyo body)

A muscle depiction study on the anime frame. The muscles are a wearable layer, the fourth wearable library beside
footwear, handwear and plating (`control/lib/graph/musculature/`: card → passes → laws → adapter): a tree of muscle
masses authored on the wearer's joints, seated on the wearer's own skin, and the skin carried out to their smooth union.
The wearer keeps its frame and proportions; where no muscle reaches, its skin does not move. One dial runs from FORM
exaggeration (a few key shapes in bodybuilder proportions, as the 3D bodies of David Production's JoJo openings) to
DETAIL exaggeration (every muscle separated, the harmony made by the shadows they collect, as Tekken's), through a
fractal articulation of the big groups. The eyes gate is the operator's.

- **The hero door's `muscleShirt`** (a card word, `'saikyo'`, or `{ card, definition, groups }`): on the lofted body
  (the tiered hero, the anime head's among them); refused on the realistic body, whose muscles are its physique. Stored
  as given; a hero without one is as it was, byte for byte.
- **The Saikyo card** (`cards.js`): hulking but lean on the anime frame, first on the large cast (Z-Fighter's male).
  Fourteen groups (the chest, the core, the flank, the back, the trapezius, the seat, the deltoid, the biceps, the
  triceps, the forearm, the elbow, the quadriceps, the hamstrings, the calf), each by level: 0 its silhouette in a few shapes, 1 its
  muscles, 2 their heads (the pectoral's fans, the eight blocks of the rectus, the serratus's fingers, the deltoid's
  three heads, the biceps' two, the triceps' horseshoe, the teardrop over the knee, the calf's diamond). A trunk mass is
  seated by its height up the torso bone and its azimuth, a limb's by its share down the bone and its azimuth round it;
  each stands `proud` of the skin, in the wearer's half biacromial.
- **The definition dial** (`definition`, 0 … 1; `principles.js`): level 0 grown at the form end; level 1 rising out of
  its parent over the first half, level 2 over the second, each parent sunk under its children as they come, so the
  silhouette holds; every level's blend tighter toward the detail end, the finest a little prouder. A group may be held
  at its own definition (`groups: { core: 1 }`).
- **The passes** (`passes.js`): each body shell re-sampled at the shirt's grain (about a centimetre) on its own smooth
  cage, its bind's shares carried as the form field's re-sampling carries them, the left limbs mirrored from the right;
  each mass seated where a ray from the bone leaves the skin; each point carried out along its ring's ray to the smooth
  union of the skin and the masses its part wears (a compact smooth minimum: past every mass's reach, exactly the skin).
  The pectoral layer is taken off (the chest group is the chest). The whole shirt costs well under a second.
- **Shells that overlap** (`adapters/loft.js`): where two shells land on the same muscle, the one that should not show
  is tucked a few millimetres in, as far as the shirt moved it (the torso and the limbs show; the neck, the pelvis, the
  thigh and the joints' bridging shells under them), and every shell's ends dive under their neighbours: the two had
  z-fought in stripes, and each shell's end stood as a rim. A limb's muscles are worn by the segment across its joint
  too, so both sides of the elbow and the knee follow one bulge.
- **The shoulder's top closed in a dome**: the shoulder's drum, its web and the arm's top ended in flat fans the shirt
  never moved, a box under the deltoid; the ends that show are closed in rings to the pole (along the part's axis, to
  70°, since the compiler winds a shell by its first band) and worn like the sides.
- **The hands follow the arms** (the operator's): each hand, its digits and their joints scaled about the wrist by three
  quarters of the forearm's growth in girth (about 1.3 on the Saikyo body), so the fingers still turn in their knuckles;
  the wrist's bridge eased from the forearm's scale to the hand's (grown whole, it stood as a cuff). A card may name its
  own scale (`hands`).
- **The chest at the detail end, rounded** (the operator's): the pectoral's heads at level 2 are a full belly low and
  in, a lower border that curves up gently and ends short of the armpit, an upper band and a round outer corner; the
  fans that had reached out to the armpit converged there in a triangle.
- **Nipples, a setting** (`nipples: true`, off by default): marks on the chest the muscles made, seated where a ray
  from the trunk's axis leaves the displaced chest and worn after the muscles, an areola and a papilla under their own
  tight blend, sized to read at the shirt's grain (one under it barely moved a point).
- **The feet follow the legs**: each foot (the shoe's two boxes, or the bare foot and its toes) and the toes' joints
  scaled about the ground under the ankle by three fifths of the shank's growth in girth (about 1.18 on the Saikyo
  body), so the sole stays on the ground. A card may name its own scale (`feet`).
- **The shoulder's cap** (with the anime frame's clavicle below, the shoulder's drums stood above the shoulder's line):
  the deltoid's crown seated above the joint on a steep ray, so the arm's dome is carried up over the shoulder as a
  round cap, its heads seated higher so no waist shows under it; the web's and the drum's tucks taken whole (they lie
  under the arm's skin, and still bridge the armpit as the arm rises); a dome's points take their tuck whole (the
  dome is the shirt's surface, none of the wearer's), and a domed end no end tuck (it had cut a groove under the dome).
- **Squash and stretch** (a group's `act`, `principles.js` `ACTIVITY` and `ACTIVITY_JOINTS`; `activity: false` holds the
  muscles as at rest): as a joint closes its flexors bunch (shorter along the fibre, fuller and deeper, prouder, the
  belly sliding toward its origin: the biceps' peak rising as the elbow closes) and its extensors stretch (longer,
  narrower, flatter: the triceps drawn long, the quadriceps over the bent knee), each about as much muscle as it was.
  The elbow (the biceps and the triceps), the knee (the hamstrings and the quadriceps) and the shoulder's raise (the
  deltoid bunching, the chest and the lats drawn long). Per joint the right side's masses are made active and the parts
  they are worn by displaced again; the difference is a CORRECTIVE on the rest (`muscleElbowR` …), the left side's its
  mirror, driven by the joint, so it rides into an export's clips as the realistic body's pauldron does. Zero at rest.
- **A bend driver** for a corrective (`driver.bend`, the joint before: `station-loft-rig.js` `correctiveWeight`,
  `body-relational-correctives.js` `correctiveRest`, the pack's driver joints): its weight the joint's flexion, the
  angle between the bone into it and the bone out of it, 0 straight. A driver without one reads the raise as before;
  the glTF's corrective note says how an engine reads it only where a target names it.
- **The skin's guards** (they came out of the raised arm): a ray that leaves no surface within its reach, or one carried
  past 6.5 cm (a ray grazing along a mass), is held at that cap (7 cm for a dome on a shell that shows); such a point
  takes no part in the elbow's or the knee's corrective (hidden in another shell at rest, posed it swung out in
  shards); the shoulder's cone and web wear only the arm's groups; a corrective's point past 8 cm, or far past its
  neighbours, left out or eased to them.
- **The form end without plates** (definition 0 had shown flat plates on the back, the thighs, the arms and the hips):
  three faults. A point carried past the cap had been put back on the skin, a patch sunk flat under the muscles round
  it, about 1,400 points at the form end, where the level-0 shapes stand furthest out; it is now held at the cap, and the
  cap is 6.5 cm, not 4.5 (the torso's, the thigh's and the shank's muscles stand a smooth 5 to 6 cm out there; the
  stray rays run on to 16). A right limb's shells had worn every group's masses, the chest's and the back's among
  them, where its squash and stretch wore only its own; they wear only their own. And where a mass meets the skin
  square on, two neighbouring points had stood centimetres apart (34 mm over one slot on the back): the skin now climbs
  onto a mass in a ramp, each point's move raised (never lowered) to its neighbours' less `SLOPE` (0.8) times their
  distance, a point held at the cap raising none. The elbow's and the knee's correctives leave the shoulder's domes
  alone (the elbow's biceps, slid toward its origin, had grazed the arm's dome and lifted it 7 cm).
- **The waist and the hip without their seams** (the operator's): the torso over the pelvis and the pelvis over the
  thighs are overlapping shells, and the shirt carries each onto the muscles along rays from its own axis, so in the
  overlap the two landed a millimetre or two apart and flickered through each other: a jagged line at the waist, the
  thigh's top in strips over the hip, the pelvis's brief outline torn. Now a shell that should not show is KEPT IN
  ORDER with the shell over it (`passes.js` `keptInOrder`): each of its points within 2 cm of that shell on the flat body
  takes the nearest place on it and sits under it there as the shirt carried it, its tuck's difference (at least 2 mm)
  below, eased to its own displacement further off; an end BURIED inside a shell that shows over it (the thigh's top in
  the pelvis, the pelvis's top in the torso, the bridges' ends) dives 8 mm over 2.5 cm (`BURIED_TUCK`), and an end that
  shows only 1.5 mm (`END_TUCK`, was 4: the torso's edge dived through the pelvis under it and crossed it in a dark
  band). The hip reads as one surface down to the pelvis's own end; a thin line stays where each shell ends.
- **The forearm's side profile, the elbow and the wrist** (the operator's): measured along the forearm's bone (front,
  back, out and in), the forearm flared 4 cm in its first 4 cm under the elbow and fell in a concave pinch to a wrist
  0.65 of the hand's width (the forearm's last ring the flat body's, the hand grown 1.3), and the elbow's bridge stood in
  a band between the upper arm and the forearm. Now: the forearm's bulk seated higher and longer; an ELBOW group of
  one level, so its landmarks hold at every definition (a level-0 mass in a deeper group sinks under its children
  toward the detail end): the brachioradialis's root rising out of the upper arm above the joint on the thumb's side, the
  olecranon the elbow's point at the back, the two epicondyles its width; the elbow's width 0.82 of the forearm's (was
  0.72), its back line from the triceps over the olecranon to the ulna without a dip. The forearm TAPERED out from its
  bone toward the hand's scale from 0.4 of the way down (`passes.js` `taperedTo`, `principles.js` `WRIST_FROM`), so the
  wrist meets the hand at 0.82 of its width; the wrist's bridge grown from its own rings' centres, its forearm end kept
  where it was along the arm (scaled about the wrist it slid over the forearm's end and flickered through it in teeth).
- **The joints' bridges welded** (`adapters/loft.js` `ABUT`, `passes.js` `welded`): the elbow's, the knee's and the wrist's
  bridges meet their neighbours ring to ring on the flat body, not overlapping; tucked under them, with their neighbours'
  ends diving, each joint showed a band and a crisp line at each ring. Now a bridge is not tucked, its neighbours' ends
  meeting it do not dive, and its end rings are carried to theirs (eased over 2.5 cm); the shells that show over others
  where they overlap are named (`OVER`: the torso over the neck and the pelvis, the pelvis over the thighs), not read
  off the tucks (by the tucks the elbow's bridge counted the pelvis it hangs beside as over it). An end counts as buried
  only 1 cm or more inside the shell over it.
- **The glutes rounded** (the operator's): the seat's side profile stood 1.7 cm off the flat body's in a flat slab from
  the hip joint's height to a ledge over the thigh. Now each cheek is a round mass, as deep as it is broad, its fibre
  slanting down and out as the gluteus maximus's does, with a lower cheek (`gluteLower`) that holds the fullest point just
  over the fold and turns the surface under into it: 4.6 cm past the lower back at the detail end, curving under over
  6 cm to the fold; the form end's one seat shape narrower and further out, so the two cheeks keep their cleft.
- **Posed: classical poses and wide stances** (the operator's): the front and back double biceps, most muscular, hands on
  hips, arms behind the head, side chest and contrapposto read clean at full figure; so do the athletic ready stance,
  the horse stance, the sumo squat, a fighting stance and a side lunge. Where the wide stances broke: the thigh's top,
  hidden under the pelvis, sheared out through the crotch and under the seat. The hidden shell had been set at the
  shell over it's offset both ways, so where the pelvis's own muscles carried it out, the thigh's top followed it out
  and, posed, came through the pelvis's hem. Now a hidden shell is only ever pulled IN (`keptInOrder`): a point the shirt
  left under the shell over it stays where it was; and away from that shell's open end it lies a further 6 mm under
  (`KEEP_DEEP`, eased in over 3 cm). Tried and set aside: giving the hidden points the outer shell's bind share
  (fewer points escaped by count, but those left tore in long shards across the groin) and fading the hold at the
  outer shell's open end (no better). Thigh points escaping the pelvis in the horse stance: about 280 → 180; the plain
  body has its own shards there, being two boxes at the crotch.
- **The hip joined** (the operator's; `passes.js` `hipWrapped`, `hipHidden`): the pelvis had been a brief over the
  thighs, each shell bound its own way (the pelvis rigid to its bone, the thigh ramping through the hip's fold to the
  femur), and in a wide stance the thighs' tops tore out through its leg openings, the plain body's as well. Now, as the
  realistic body hands its hip over, by one level: the pelvis's rings under the hip joint are re-laid round the union
  of itself and both thighs (each slot the farthest crossing along its azimuth from the trunk's axis), so the pelvis
  wraps the tops of both legs as one surface down to a level 1.2 cm over the crotch, where the thighs take the skin; its
  lowest ring goes on straight down a little inside them and its cap closes over the crotch (drawn sharply in, it had
  shaded the level's ring into a dark band). Out at the sides the wrap takes the weights of the thigh under it at its
  height (the hip's fold, then the femur), none on the midline (`HIP_SIDE`), so it moves with the legs. Each thigh is
  drawn 6 mm in from half a band under the level (hidden under the wrap, crossing it at a slope rather than lying on it
  in teeth), and under the level its skin facing out from the trunk is eased out to the wrap's lowest ring over 4 cm
  where that stands at most 2.5 cm further out (`HIP_DROP`, `HIP_REACH`: the cheek's underside running into the thigh;
  without the reach, the inner thigh's front was drawn out to the belly's front at the crotch and spiked posed). The
  thigh is no longer kept under the pelvis (`OVER`), the wrap does that. At rest the hip reads as one surface: the
  cheeks round under into the gluteal fold, a thin line where the shells meet; the ready, horse and sumo stances, the
  fighting stance and the side lunge hold at the crotch at both ends of the dial.
- **The Saikyo body's female** (the operator's; `cards.js` `saikyo-female`, and `saikyo` on a female wearer): muscular
  and athletic on the anime frame's female, its silhouette and definition read off a heroic female in a superhero
  brawler's art seen from behind: a broad, capped shoulder over sweeping lats and a deep erector channel, the waist held
  narrow (the obliques and the core lower and flatter), the seat full, round and high with the medius's shelf at the
  hip's side, the hamstrings and the adductors filling the thigh's back and inside, the vastus's sweep, diamond calves, a
  full triceps over a leaner biceps. Built from the male's card group by group (`restyled`: a group's proud and radii
  scaled, masses left out or retuned, `each` and `shift` for one mass or the whole group's seats), its masses in her own
  half biacromial (about 0.69 of his). Her BUST is a group of its own (`bust`), one level, so it holds at every
  definition, broad and deep so it rounds out of the chest; her pectoral is seated high and out above it. The shirt takes
  the authored pectoral layer off, and the male's fans worn in its place had stood as a man's chest. Her lower ab row
  and lower rectus are left out (on her shorter trunk they landed on the lower belly as a pair of blocks); her knee's
  teardrop and the calf's form-end mass are held in (her knee is slimmer than his, and they ballooned into a ball). The
  door passes the hero's cast (`muscleShirt(recipe, spec, { cast })`; a card may carry `casts`), and a spec's `groups`
  may name a cast's groups (`bust`).
- **Body codenames, each a dyad** (the operator's: "the muscular form and the simplified muscular form share the same
  base"; `polygonizer/anime-bodies.js`, the hero door's `animeBody`): a codename names a body on the anime frame, worn
  two ways. Its SIMPLIFIED form is a body tune laid in place of the head style's body (the style's head size kept, the
  hero's own tune and a look composing over it as before), so any anime head wears any body of its pole; its MUSCULAR
  form is the `muscleShirt` over that same base, wearing the codename's own card when the shirt names none. The door
  stores the word beside a resolved stamp (`animeBodyResolved`, as `animeStyleResolved`), refuses a word of the other
  pole and one without the anime head. TOJI (male) and MIZUKI (female) are the base: Z-Fighter's bodies, so a hero that
  names them draws as a Z-Fighter hero does, and their cards are the Saikyo cards (`toji`, `mizuki`; `saikyo` the same
  by its old name). SATORU (male, slim): a tall, long-limbed swimmer's V, near Shonen High's size and set apart from it
  by height in the legs and a broad shoulder over a narrow waist; his card the base's muscles lean and dry (every mass
  0.62 as proud and 0.92 as large, the lats and the shoulder's cap kept fuller for the V, the arms and the chest the
  leanest). MAKI (female, slim): an athlete near Shonen High's size, a squarer shoulder, a held waist, fuller thighs
  and calves; her card Mizuki's muscles lean (0.65, 0.93), her seat, hamstrings and calves kept fuller, her bust held.
  A slim card is the base's `slimmed` (musculature/cards.js). ARMSTRONG (male, hulking): a strongman-bodybuilder's
  mass, taller and far heavier than Toji, the neck buried in the yoke, the shoulders and the chest's depth at their
  widest, the arms and legs massive; his card the base's massed (1.28 as proud, 1.07 as large; the yoke, the chest and
  the arms the most). KALE (female, hulking): a powerhouse, broad in the shoulder and the hip, the arms and legs
  massive; her card Mizuki's massed, the back, the seat and the legs the most, her bust held as Mizuki's. On both the
  deltoid's crown over the shoulder's top is held near the base's (massed with the heads, it carried the arm's dome past
  the move's cap, held flat there); and the shells under the arm's skin are tucked in proportion to the arm's girth
  over Toji's (`UNDER_GIRTH`: Armstrong's web stood level with the arm's dome). Mizuki's rectus sheet is held short
  and raised (its lower end had stood on her lower belly as a pair of blocks, the plainer on Kale).
- **The clothes over the shirt** (the operator's: "the muscular figures are literally ripping through their shirts";
  found merging with the anime-7g consolidation, which carries the dressing work; `passes.js` `clothedOver`,
  `garmentDense`, `repinned`): every garment, kit and adornment is built from the plain body before the shirt runs, so
  the muscles came through the cloth, hems and boots stayed where the lengthened legs no longer were, and anything pinned
  to the body's faces (an adornment, a clothed detail's creases, a stud on a shirt) failed to build. Now the shirt
  dresses its own body:
  - **Fitted over the muscle**: each garment (`<piece>_<part>`, its body part named, `CLOTH_OVER` the shells its cloth
    lies over there) is re-sampled at the shirt's grain (between its own coarse rings a flat face had cut under the
    muscle's bumps; its run taken from 0, a vest's started at 1.4 and folded inside out) and each point carried out along
    its ring's ray over the muscled skin under it, keeping the room it had over the plain body (at least 4 mm, at most
    2 cm: a layer keeps its order over another, a loose one is pushed only where the muscle comes within its room). The
    highest muscle within 2.5 cm to the side holds the cloth, so a groove narrower than the cloth's span is bridged.
  - **A skirt hangs**: a closed shell down its outside and back up its inside; its outside falls straight from its widest
    point (each ring at least as far out as the one over it), its inside carried out with it, keeping its thickness.
  - **With the legs, the hands and the feet**: a garment on a leg stretches with it, a shoe or a glove grows with the
    foot or the hand.
  - **The body's flex on the cloth**: each garment point takes the corrective offsets of the body point under it.
  - **Pins found again**: a pinned part's place on its parent as it was found on the parent re-sampled, the nearest face
    and its weights, so it rides where the shirt carried that face. An adornment and a clothed detail are worn with the
    shirt again.
- **The legs lengthened**- **The legs lengthened** (the operator's: the hands and the feet grown with the arms and the legs read the figure
  stocky; `passes.js` `lengthened`, a card's `legs`, the Saikyo cards' 1.06): the leg's shells, its joints and the pelvis
  stretched up from the ankle to the hip joint, everything over the hip lifted by as much (about 5 cm), so the soles stay
  on the ground and the figure stands taller in the legs, where a heroic figure takes its height; the hanging hands lift
  with the arms rather than stretch, the head's pinned meshes ride the cranium, and the hip's fold's axis grows with the

- **The hip wrap over high thighs**: the wrap re-lays the pelvis's rings up to the hip joint, or past it to over the

- **The hip's side in an abducted stance** (the operator's): the handover rises toward the outer hip (`HIP_RISE`,

- **The glutes in a squat** (the operator's): squash and stretch at the HIP (`principles.js` `ACTIVITY_JOINTS.hip`, driven

- **Held** (`musculature.test.js`): the dial's laws; absence adds nothing (a skin no mass reaches keeps every point);
